description: There is an enchantment which you may cast upon your units without economic repercussions from its upkeep. You can always cancel an enchantment later.
instruction: Select to open Spells.
title: Strengthen Armies with Enchantments

description:
You can now acquire your first empire skill.

Empire skills can provide you with some powerful bonuses and shape the progression of your Empire. Your Affinity will unlock new empire skills over time. You can then spend Imperium to acquire them.
instruction: Left-click to check the Empire Skill tree
title: Choose your first Empire Skill

description:
Your Empire is running out of Gold.

Unit Upkeep, Unit, and City Structure in the Production Queue may affect the amount of gold at your disposal.

Try to expand your Domain and build Province Improvement or City Structures that can provide you with additional gold per Turn.
instruction: Select to open your Throne City panel
title: Running out of Gold

description:
It's time to recruit a new Hero!

Heroes are powerful units, able to settle new Outpost and lead your Army in battle. They also provide useful bonuses to the City they are assigned to as a Governor.

To recruit heroes, your hero capacity needs to expand, which will happen over time. You can spend Imperium to increase it immediately.
instruction: Left-click to open your Throne City panel
title: Time to recruit a new Hero!

description:
You seem to have a lot of Imperium at your disposal.

Imperium can be spent to help the growth of your Empire in different ways:Acquire empire skills.Boost Allegiance with a Free City to speed up the pace at which you can rank up your diplomatic Relations.Found new City to gain control over certain parts of the map and expand the reach of your empire.Buy Population from your cities.
title: Invest your Imperium

description:
{LowFoodCity.Name} is suffering from low Food income.

Food regulates the pace at which each City can get new Population and so annex new Province. Population Upkeep requires food and may be the cause of such a shortage.

Some City Structure and Province Improvement can increase the amount of food that a city produces per Turn.
instruction: Select to go to <eventColor>{LowFoodCity.Name}</eventColor>
title: <eventColor>{LowFoodCity.Name}</eventColor> has low food income

description:
Your empire's Gold income is low.

With a low gold income, you will soon not be able to sustain your empire's needs.

Unit Upkeep can often be a common cause of low gold income. Try to expand your Domain and build Province Improvement or build City Structure in your City that can provide you with additional gold per Turn.
instruction: Select to open your Throne City panel
title: Low Gold income

description:
Your empire's Mana income is low.

With low mana income, you will soon not be able to sustain your empire's needs.

Units with Unit Enchantment can often be a common cause of low mana income. Try to expand your Domain and build Province Improvement or build City Structure that can provide you with additional mana per turn.
instruction: Select to open your Throne City panel
title: Low Mana income

description:
{LowStabCity.Name} has low City Stability.

Stability dictates how much control you have over a City. The higher the stability, the better the bonus. With negative stability, also comes troublesome events, like Unrest or Rioting.

Each Province Improvement decreases the amount of stability by a small amount. Some City Structure, such as a tavern, increase stability.
instruction: Select to go to <eventColor>{LowStabCity.Name}</eventColor>
title: <eventColor>{LowStabCity.Name}</eventColor> has low stability

description:
Your Empire is running out of Mana.

Unit Upkeep, recently cast Spell, or Unit Enchantment may affect the amount of mana at your disposal.

Try to expand your Domain and build Province Improvement or City Structure in your City that can provide you with additional mana per turn.
instruction: Select to open your Throne City panel
title: Running out of Mana

description:
There is an infestation closing in on your border. While for now it might only send raiding parities, once it overlaps your territory, the patrols will start burning these provinces down as well. The damage done by such infestations can be extensive, so take care.
Infestations can be slowed down by destroying their patrol stacks, but to ultimately deal with it you must destroy the Infestation Spawner.
instruction: Select to go to the Infestation
title: Dangerous Infestation

description:
A Free City is available for negotiations.

Negotiations will improve their Allegiance to you. As a Free City gains a higher Allegiance to you, you will form pacts that benefit your empire.

Give a Whispering Stones to {VarHouse.Name} to start negotiations.
instruction: Select to go to the Free City
title: Free City available for negotiations

description:
A hero would like to join the ranks of your empire!

Heroes are powerful units, able to settle new Outpost and lead your Army in battle. They also provide useful bonuses to the city they are assigned to as a Governor.
instruction: Left-click to go to the Hero acquisition Panel
title: A Hero can now join your Empire!

instruction: instruction test
title: <eventColor>{CityNewProv.Name}</eventColor> can annex a new Province

description:
You can assign a Hero as a Governor to one of your City.

A governor provides your Empire and the city they are assigned to with additional bonuses and Resource income.
instruction: Left-click to go to your Hero
title: A Hero can be assigned as Governor

description:
Your Ruler, {RulerDead.Name}, has perished in Combat.

Your Ruler is the most important unit of your Empire, since they allow you to cast Spell in and out of combat. Additionally, when your Ruler is dead, your Research progress will be halted.

If your Throne City is taken while your Ruler is dead, you will be defeated.

Your Ruler will stay in the void for 3 Turn, before being brought back to life in your Throne City.
instruction: Select to check on <eventColor>{RulerDead.Name}</eventColor>
title: <eventColor>{RulerDead.Name}</eventColor> has been killed

description:
An Outpost of yours can be upgraded into a City.

Select the outpost and spend Imperium to start founding the city. The outpost will take 3 Turn to upgrade into a city.
title: Outpost can be upgraded into a City

description:
It's time to expand your Empire.

In order to build new City, you have to settle an Outpost first.

Position your Ruler or one of your Hero on the center of a Province and settle your first outpost by spending {amount} Gold. An Outpost needs {amount2} Turn in order to be settled.
instruction: Left-click to go to your Ruler
title: Expand your Empire

bio:
Frikka is an ancient Godir in the guise of a Halfling, with a penchant for cunning and frivolity. Her sharp mind and quicker wit are testament to the time spent learning from the Archons before their withdrawal. Ever a fickle being, her motivations are as changeable as the winds. Mischief and mayhem are interchangeable with seemingly selfless acts of kindness that leave those who deal with her reeling with confusion and reaching for an understanding that is simply unattainable!

The Gleeful Miscreants are the aptly named race of rat-like folk that worship Frikka as master and muse. They delight in the mischief she is so talented in sowing and will, at her behest, occasionally pretend to capture her in order to lure in hapless would-be rescuers. Like Frikka herself, their looks often serve to deceive those who gaze upon them and see only helpless vermin.

The cruelest Dark Elf assassins revere this Godir, Dancer of Death, Melenis. Once the lithe mistress to Prince Meandor, she died and rose a deadly creature of undeath. Vanquished in that form, she revived anew as queen to Dark Elf assassins. Some say her mad dance between life and death leaves her fixated upon vengeance. Her bitter life taught her that all succumb to death and only fools dare hope.

These sinister Undead Lichbringers seek to master the ghastly secrets of their deadly mistress, Melenis. They tread a trail of stolen lives, steeped in tragedy. They know of no atrocity that will stay their hand from the relentless pursuit of life and death and unlife and undeath, through cultic means and forbidden lore.

A spinner of exquisite crafting, she sings a luring melody from the hidden place, feeling the vibrations in the strings of her many tangled web. The weaver Arachna spins intrigue, ensnaring lost souls that wander into darkness to hide their shame. Her dark servants move about the world, while she lurks deep in the nest of shadows.

Arachna discovered that some Goblins were so distasteful that her beloved spiders refused to consume them. With that, her Reclusive Spiderlings were born. These symbiotic fiends love lurking unnoticed in the recesses of the world. They breed their arachnids, which have now grown to such enormous proportions that they ride them into combat.

An attractive elf who nevertheless evokes an aura of haughty superiority, Cinren wears a perpetual sneer of lecherous intent. It is said that he has devoted much of his existence to the magical honing of carnal delights, often careening down dark and morally ambiguous pathways in order to reach undiscovered realms of pleasure.

The group of elves known as the Ashborn Hedonists follow Cinren Toliath and revere his godlike pursuit of pleasure. Powerful practitioners of magic in their own right, they seek to bring all under the sway of their master in order to provide more fodder towards his lecherous machinations.

Once, Otto was Nimue's eighth favorite, and for a short while everything was good. Being abandoned by his Goddess initiated his ascension to Godirhood, although he fears what these powers may do to him. Now he leads the people who call themselves Recreants, wearing the shame of Nimue's abandonment as a banner. Whether Godirhood is a blessing or a curse to the created Otto… only time will tell.

The Drowned Recreants were once named Nimue's Chosen Children and a friend to beast and man alike. They were loved by their Goddess, and they loved her in return. She, however, eventually grew disappointed with their flaws and discarded them, drowning many in her wrath. Now, those who remain call themselves the Drowned Recreants and are trying to start a civilization of their own, though many still fear the wrath of their former Goddess.

Once a proud and powerful Elven Empress beside her husband Inioch, Eleanor perished giving birth to her son, Prince Meandor. Her soul wandered to <hyperlink>Auldweald</hyperlink>, where a tomb was created to honor her, protecting her from the ills the origin world of the Elves had to endure.

Once the uncontested sovereign of the Valley of Wonders, Inioch refused to yield to the divine contracts that anointed his divine right to rule. Turning against all that was holy, he plumbed the depths of death. Now, he is little but a fragmented soul, unable to reach the Well of Creation and what lies beyond.

The name Khir Uranon has often been spoken in dreaded whisper. Those that know his name know him to be a demonic manipulator, whose mastery of the forge is fueled by a callous disregard for the souls he infuses his creations with.

The Blackfurred Forgelings are known for their prodigious strength and merciless cruelty, both aspects forged in the fires of their masters' ancient crucibles. Here, they help him utilize the souls of those that fall before them to power demonic artifacts.

Rumors surround the origins of enigmatic Lithyl Nightweaver, the half-masked wizard who seemed to appear from the Astral Void itself. Shortly after her arrival on Magehaven she joined the Shad'rai on their quest for power over others. Charming and conniving, she seems to be one of many mad Godir, haunted by her Torment of Shadows. But Lithyl specifically stands out for her talent of appearing and disappearing at opportune times.

Not all who wander the Astral Sea are Godir. Many mortals find themselves lost in its depths, forgotten, with no divine power to save them. One Godir has taken it upon herself to save these lost souls. Lithyl Nightweaver reaches out an eldritch hand to pull the Forgotten Ones from the void, no matter how haunted and scarred it left them. Whatever her ulterior motives may be, Lithyl has won her people's undying devotion.

Decimus was hand-picked by Nimue as a Ruler of her then latest created race, and proudly named Nimue's tenth favorite. He wore this honor with pride and responsibility, until his creator Goddess grew disappointed with him and his people for reasons unknown to any but herself. It was this guilt that led him to pursue a life of righteousness for him and his people, and it was this weight of responsibility that started him on his path to ascension.

The Atoning Toadmen were created by Nimue and once rose above many others, but must now answer for their sins. What sins and how, they are not sure, but they must atone nonetheless, and lead others on the same path of righteousness before their former Goddess, Nimue, can love them again.

A harbinger of intrigue, Meandor is the first Prince of the ancient tradition of Dark Elves. He plots against allies and enemies alike. He once experienced death and found it unsatisfying. He now respects his sister Julia, but won't hesitate to stab a dagger through her plans. His followers see him as a symbol of vengeance, but he prefers to shirk ideologies. He revels in remaining a wild card in the realm of diplomatic games. Yet, he, too, is haunted by his own demons.

Dark Elves lurk in the deep shadows, plotting vengeance upon humanity and the fair races that tolerate them. They will never forget how men stole their lands. Dark Elves enslave weaker races and train them in cruelty, using them to achieve their nefarious purposes. They are masters of stealth, known to favor a well placed blade in the back over a fair fight.

Since his return to Magehaven, after the events on Auldweald, Meandor has demonstrated much responsibility and leadership in the attempts of the Covenant to bring structure and order to the Godir of Magehaven. None of this he would openly admit however, as he still prefers to be regarded as a lord of shadow and death.

The Swarming Hammers emerged in a frenzy when the influence of the Chaos Endailon had stirred up war on many worlds. When they became denounced as pests that the Godir should eradicate, Meandor stepped in to take them under his care. Through him they learned to channel their ceaseless energy into the creation of monumental structures and rune-enchanted artisanry. Though Meandor seeks to mentor them into independence, ruled by a champion of their own, the Swarming Hammers still revere him as their swarm king, eager to pave any way he desires to walk.

Her mind is a torrent of unpredictable chaos. She wills it and her children rise from the surge, breathing her very lifeblood. Like the tide beating against the changing coastline, so too is Nimue among the Godir. Her power is undeniable, yet her moods swirl like waves in a tide pool. Her children all accept that, inevitably, all will find themselves drowned in a watery grave.

Obsequious and ever condescending, Nimue's Chosen Children know that their time as her favored creations is limited, and if they're not careful, they will all end up drowned in the depths. Fortunately, these clever amphibians have an affinity for water, and know ways of quietly slipping beneath the surface when her storms start churning up the muck.

Saridas was once a Dark Elven advisor to Prince Meandor. Later, he married Queen Julia, thus becoming king of the High Elves on Athla. He suffered dearly from the loss of his only son, Thannis, and almost threw his empire into an all-out war. His quest for vengeance only stopped due to his own daughter, Sundren. Of course, the life of a king is never safe... and in the years following the Third Age, Saridas found his demise after the seals of Athla were broken. His soul traveled to <hyperlink>Auldweald</hyperlink> where he was reunited with his son. Now, he is forced to stay on this realm until a Godir breaks the curse that affects it.

Shira was born the heir of her people. During her coronation, the Shad'rai invaded her realm, killed her family and cast her into the Astral Void. Shira would have been Lost if not for the aid of Meandor, who guided her to Magehaven, where she joined the Covenant and learned to channel her grief into primal prowess. After a heroic return and a fierce battle against the usurping Shad'rai Godir, she retook her homeland.

Arctic Felines are a proud people who adjusted to the icy tundra of Cantarra, their homeworld. After the return of their long-lost Queen, they followed her through the depths of the Astral Sea and back to avenge their fallen royal family and thwart the plans of the Shad'rai.

Curious and clever, Sundren was the second-born child, daughter of Queen Julia and her royal consort. She founded the Torchbearers as one of the few leaders ever to unite High Elves with their Dark-Elf kindred... But after the assassination of her brother, and later the death of her father, Sundren finds her noble heart growing dark with a lust for vengeance.

Mended Torchbearers are the kindred and followers of Sundred and her dream of a life filled with a deeply heroic meaning. Many kindred were once jaded by age and propriety, while others thirsted for bloody revenge. Sundren gave them all a much more thrilling reason to live.

Many mourn the loss of the High Elven prodigy, Thannis, the first High Elf born on Athla after the mending of the Dark and Wood Elves. His unjustified death caused empires to clash and threw Athla into an all-out war, only brought to an end by the heroic actions of his rebellious sister, Sundren. His soul wandered to <hyperlink>Auldweald</hyperlink>, the origin world of all Elves, where he remains, not necessarily voluntarily.

Stare into the flames long enough and a single name will come to your lips. A god of fire. Only a god of fire can live within the raging inferno, able to master its unpredictable flow of destruction. He is quick to punish those that do not give him rightful reverence, for only creatures that can withstand waves of unrelenting heat are worthy to serve the great Godir, Yaka.

Remembering a time when felines were worshiped as god-kin, the Firebrand Predators serve Yaka with a zeal that he has not seen for generations. Yaka dotes upon his Tigran followers, for he remembers how his past servants abandoned him. Together they seek to build an unquenchable inferno.

A mighty Orc whose honor-bound convictions match his prodigious strength, Turiel was the first Wizard King to ascend to Godirhood. He appears as a mighty and masked Orc, a bastion of stoic ferocity clad in indomitable armor and wielding brutal weaponry. Ever oath-bound to the Archon in guarding Grexolis, he holds honor and duty in highest esteem.

Turiel leads the mighty Onmar, fierce Ascended Orcs who aid him in a duty shared and who have, in return, been blessed by the Archon. Their minds are guarded against the insidious whispers of the banished souls they hold eternal vigil over.

Like the Void Stone that replaced his heart through a macabre covenant for power, Ydgaard's desires run to the cold and shiny. A grizzled and mighty Dwarf whose greed is as impressive as his beard, he covets wealth and resources above all. The great jewel that adorns his left eye socket in place of an eyeball (also part of the aforementioned pact) is a stark reflection of how he sees the world.

Ydgaard rules over a race of mole-like beings known as the Grave Underlings. It is surmised that their form was chosen due in part to their poor eyesight, that they may never covet their master's wealth. Likewise, their natural predilection to excavation of the planet's riches allow them to ever increase the size of Ydgaard's own hoard.

description: It was the time when the raw forces of magic returned to Athla. The seal that had protected the world was shattered, the cosmic currents thereby unleashed shaped the land, changing what was whilst returning what once may have been. In the wake of this new genesis, the great empires of the Third Age fell into decline, bringing on an era of re-exploration and expansion.

Alas, the time for peaceful discovery was brief, for the ancient wizards of the Second Age broke free from their eldritch prisons in the depths of the Astral Sea. Their strength regained, they set out to rule over the surviving peoples as god-kings, or Godir.

There was little divine about them. Yaka, Nimue, Karissa—a pantheon of pretender gods. They were scarred, corrupted, haunted by millennia of torment—and ready to unleash their newfound powers against whoever dared stand in their way.
Yet the Wizard Kings were not unchallenged. Mortal champions rose to the defense of their people, rebuilding their realms and learning to channel the currents of magic.

This is the story of one such champion. While traveling through the Valley of Wonders in search of a new home, tragedy befell <<o:HeroFirstName>> tribe, its elder slain by a magical being. After inheriting both the elder’s throne and his powerful Tome of Magic, the young champion had to rise up and protect <<o:HeroFirstName>> people from the dangers that awaited them.

By repelling the invasion of Yaka, the spark of divinity was ignited, and a new Godir ascended to the cosmic Pantheon. Beyond the veil of mortality, the Pantheon represented an entirely different world. For while the Godir could walk the realms as gods, they had to abide by rules when dealing with their own kin within the Astral Sea.

In Magehaven, a world near the center of the Astral Sea, the Godir of the Pantheon had established their forum of counsel. It was a place warded by an ancient spell. Stripped of their abilities to harm one another, even the fiercest enemies could meet up in Magehaven. Here the Godir constructed their World Gates, through which they embarked on their journeys of exploration and expansion that defined the Fourth Age of Wonders.

As a mortal champion, build up a new home for your wandering tribe in the mythical Valley of Wonders. Prepare yourself for the clash with the returning Wizard Kings of old and rise in power to claim a greater destiny.
name: Valley of Wonders
sub_header: As an <hyperlink>Ascended Champion</hyperlink>, build up a new home for your wandering tribe in the mythical <hyperlink>Valley of Wonders</hyperlink> on <hyperlink>Athla</hyperlink>. Prepare yourself for the clash with the returning <hyperlink>Wizard King</hyperlink> of old and rise in power to claim a greater destiny.

description: The Astral Sea connects all and everything. To most, it is merely a way to travel between worlds, yet some call the Astral Sea itself their home. Of the many beings who reside within, the curious Maer are the most gentle. They swim through the magical currents with ease and use their voices to guide lost souls to safety. This is the story of one such Maer called Elya, whose curiosity led her to misery.
title: The Maer

description: This particular young Maer was intrigued by the worlds that connect to the Astral Sea. She was specifically attracted to a realm called the Enchanted Archipelago, for its tides resembled her natural habitat, yet felt so different. But it did not take long before Elya's visit turned into a nightmare, when she was captured by a capricious Godir called Nimue who sought to study her for her beauty and power.
title: Capture

description: The self-proclaimed "Goddess" Nimue used Elya in her efforts to create her ultimate race of followers… but her results never lived up to her ever-shifting demands. Elya was forced to watch Nimue drown her own creations over and over again, only to begin anew once more. The horrified Elya, shackled and sequestered, could only sing a desperate song, carried by the currents over the Astral Sea.
title: A Desperate Song

description: Elya's song reached Magehaven, where the Covenant, a virtuous alliance of Godir, heard her plea. The Covenant sought to uphold the ancient agreements of peace and stability, and were thus concerned by the song about Nimue. Had the Siren Goddess gone mad with power, or was another force at play? One zealous Godir of the Covenant volunteered to investigate the Enchanted Archipelago and liberate it from Nimue's drowning embrace.
title: The Savior

description: Thus was the Siren Goddess defeated and the Enchanted Archipelago freed from her obsessive grasp. And Elya, the curious Maer who euphorically experienced freedom once more… I am her. It was I who witnessed both the terror and grace of the Godir. It is for this reason that I sing the stories of this Age of Godir and of the good and the evil that reside within the ever-flowing Astral Sea.
title: The Goddess, Defeated

description: Yet my freedom begets responsibility. I could no longer ignore the murder and destruction of the powerless and innocent. My time as prisoner taught me about the plans of Nimue and her allies, the Godir alliance who call themselves the Shad'rai. This is why I had to inform the Covenant about the scheming Shad'rai and their ambitions—which were far greater than what the Covenant imagined.
title: Dark Plans

description: Become an ambassador of the Covenant and venture to the Enchanted Archipelago, where a once Banished Wizard is abusing the currents of Creation. Investigate the goals of the Shad'rai alliance and free the realm from the Siren Goddess.
name: Enchanted Archipelago
sub_header: Become an ambassador of the <hyperlink>Covenant</hyperlink> and venture to the Enchanted Archipelago on <hyperlink>Tidolon</hyperlink>, where a once banished <hyperlink>Wizard King</hyperlink> is abusing the currents of Creation. Investigate the goals of the <hyperlink>Shad'rai</hyperlink> alliance and free the realm from the Siren Goddess.

description: Ages ago, when the Astral Sea was still young, the Archons created a magical artifact. Forged in the fires of an Elder Dragon, the Gildercoil served as an arcane compass, guiding the Archons through the currents between realms. According to legend, it still contains the echoes of their arcane journeys, and can lead those who hold it to forgotten places of sealed knowledge and magic.
title: Visions of Sand

description: With its mysterious promise of power, the Gildercoil fanned the greed of many rulers, until a daring Godir betrayed the Archons and stole the Gildercoil from their Celestial Reliquary. Ever since then, all traces of the compass have been lost, as have those of the cunning thief who disappeared into the mists of time.
title: The False God

description: Or so it seemed for many a lifetime... Lithyl Nightweaver was the first of the Shad'rai to find clues of the Gildercoil's whereabouts—myths, leading to runic omens, leading to riddles. The Shad'rai were persistent in their search, for too well did the Archon artifact fit into their unfolding plans. And they were rewarded.
name: Crimson Caldera

description: In the infernal world of Obbadoth, there exists a realm known as the Crimson Caldera, where war is eternal. Here the Gildercoil lay hidden. Yet the Shad'rai sought no open conflict with Obbadoth's demonic princes. As they weighed their options, an ambitious Godir from their ranks volunteered to venture there alone, well aware of the prestige and power that could be gained within their order.

Thus, by the hands of the Shad'rai, the wicked scheme of Frikka Dynosis had been revealed, and the Gildercoil was recovered. The Crimson Caldera had met its champion and even the princes of Obbadoth dared not interfere.
title: Chaos Mission Debriefing 01

description: As an agent of the Shad'rai, venture to a demonic realm of never-ending war to search for an ancient Archon artifact of power. Become the victor in an arena of mad violence and end the curse that brought doom upon so many aspiring kings and Godir.
sub_header: As an agent of the <hyperlink>Shad'rai</hyperlink>, venture to a demonic realm of never-ending war to search for an ancient <hyperlink>Archon</hyperlink> artifact of power. Become the victor in an arena of mad violence and end the curse of <hyperlink>Obbadoth</hyperlink>, which brought doom upon so many aspiring kings and <hyperlink>Godir</hyperlink>.

title: The Shad'rai Plot: Smelter Mountains (Ertra Anov)

description: After seizing the Gildercoil, the Shad'rai suddenly disappeared. This concerned most Godir, the members of the Covenant in particular, who were actively opposed to the Shad'rai and their schemes. However, none knew how to follow the Shad'rai, or what their destination was. The Covenant convened in Magehaven to debate.
title: Concern amongst the Covenant

description: The Athlan ruler Sundren proposed to seek out Prince Meandor, her uncle. Meandor was a powerful Wizard of Death and the heir of the fallen House Inioch. He was the first Athlan to discover Magehaven and had guided many banished wizards there, including the Shad'rai, saving them from eternal torment in the darkness that lay between the realms. If anyone could track down the Shad'rai wizards, it was Meandor.
title: Prince of Shadows

description: However, for reasons unknown or unfortunate, Meandor had elected to exile himself to Auldweald, the ancient home world of the Elves, where he established a realm for himself. Since then, concerning reports had reached Magehaven. The shadow of death had washed over the vibrant forests, its cities haunted by lingering souls and roaming spirits who were unable to finish their journeys to the Well of Creation.
title: Eternal Court

description: Many Elves had since fled the realm, reporting that Meandor was responsible for its fall. He had vowed to restore his beloved lost Elven Court to its old glory. Dark magic followed him and his apparitions as he turned the realm itself against anyone who dared enter his waking dream of the past. The Covenant saw no choice but to send a fearless Godir to reclaim this Eternal Court from the renegade Wizard of Shadows.
title: A Ghostly Curse

description: A fearless Godir of the Covenant broke Meandor's curse and freed the souls trapped within the Eternal Court. After his recovery in Magehaven, Meandor explained he had uncovered the plans of the Shad'rai and their search for the Gildercoil. The Covenant's concerns about the Shad'rai were justified, for the Gildercoil was not just a compass… It was a powerful Archon artifact, capable of leading those wielding it to powers even legends dared not mention.

The Shad'rai sought to release the power locked away by the Archons. They had invited Meandor to join their cause, but after his refusal, the dark cabal had ensnared him in the nightmares of his past. Meandor was furious that he had allowed himself to be manipulated. He thus decided to aid the Covenant and used his strong connection to the Astral Sea to locate the Shad'rai. But before the other Godir could follow, he issued a warning.

After spending an age clinging to the past, Meandor concluded that the flow of the Astral Sea could not be compelled or defied. He sensed anticipation within the currents: forces from the dawn of time would imminently resurface. The Shad'rai may have been unscrupulous in their search for this power but, deep down, all Godir lust for it. Meandor bitterly declared that a Godir has but one choice: Follow the pulls of the tide... or seek oblivion, as he did.

Join the Covenant once more to investigate the haunted forests of the Auldweald, origin world of the Elves. Confront the mad Wizard who has cast the realm into the shadows of undeath and free the trapped spirits within.
name: The Eternal Court
sub_header: Join the <hyperlink>Covenant</hyperlink> once more to investigate the haunted forests of <hyperlink>Auldweald</hyperlink>, origin world of the elves. Confront the mad <hyperlink>Wizard King</hyperlink> who has cast the realm into the shadows of undeath, and free the trapped <hyperlink>Souls</hyperlink> within.

description: "Glory to all Godir and glory to the Shad'rai!" The rousing hymn of the Shad'rai was heard far and wide as they gathered to use the Gildercoil and embark from Magehaven to challenge the Archons themselves. For too long had archaic Archon dogmas controlled the cosmos and determined what should exist and what shouldn't. It was time to ring in a new age and break the chains that fettered the true potential of the Pantheon.
title: Grexolis

description: Grexolis was the long-sought-after target of the Shad'rai. It was a world whose mere existence had been concealed by the Archons in great effort, as it contained the forbidden magic of ancient times. The Gildercoil not only guided the Shad'rai to Grexolis—it was the very key to opening the World Vault itself. Coming to Grexolis meant to seek celestial judgment. But the Shad'rai were prepared.

The battle had been fierce, but at last the Shad'rai overwhelmed the Covenant and Turiel, guardian of Grexolis. Their victory, however, became tainted with confusion when Lithyl Nightweaver revealed her true identity. And then, she broke the World Vault. Grexolis burst open in a swirl of raw magic, an arcane tide surging through the Astral Sea. In the blink of an eye, entire worlds came to be anew while a myriad of forgotten thoughts invaded the minds of the present Godir.

As the turmoil slowly subsided, the Shad'rai convened on the empty shell of Grexolis to reflect on their achievement. They had caught a glimpse of something great, a veil lifted on ancient times and its primal gods. Forgotten were all worries about the Archons and their distant war with the Shadow. For the realms of the altered cosmos glimmered like beacons of magic mystery—as if they were beckoning Magehaven's Godir to rise in this Fourth Age of Wonders.

As the spearhead of a Shad'rai alliance, invade the fractured world Grexolis hidden in the mists of the Astral Sea. Face the custodian, whom the Archons left on this world to guard the ancient magic which lies buried here.
name: Grexolis
sub_header: As the spearhead of a <hyperlink>Shad'rai</hyperlink> alliance, invade the fractured world <hyperlink>Grexolis</hyperlink> hidden in the mists of the <hyperlink>Astral Sea</hyperlink>. Face the custodian, which the <hyperlink>Archons</hyperlink> left on this world to guard the ancient magic which lies buried here.

description: All attacking units gain extra <hyperlink>Hs defense defense</hyperlink> against <eventColor>{GLOBAL.RetaliationConcept.Name}</eventColor>.
name: Retrain Troops

description: Continuous rain makes all units <hyperlink>Wet</hyperlink>.
name: Rainfall

description: There are several extra <hyperlink>Obscuring</hyperlink> Flora Obstacles present in combat.
name: Rampant Flora

description: This location has been razed or raided. Many obstacles are damaged, destroyed, or on fire.
name: Razed

description:
Several traps have been revealed on the map! If a unit moves over them, it will be inflicted with Bleeding for 3 Turn and reveal the trap!

Does not affect Floating movement, Flying movement, or Ethereal units.
name: Revealed Traps

description: The attacker has seized control of the ritual! In 5 <turn></turn>, a <hyperlink>Balor</hyperlink> with <hyperlink>Berserk</hyperlink> will join the attacker until the end of battle.
Each 2 <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink>, one of the attacking units has a 90% base chance of suffering <hyperlink>Distracted</hyperlink> until the end of combat.
name: Distracting Whispers

description: The duelist takes reduced damage from all units, except from the stack leader of the opposing army.
name: Duelist's Protection

description: The attacking armies <hyperlink>Expeditionleader</hyperlink> <hyperlink>Taunt</hyperlink> the Silver Knight until the end of the battle.
name: Taunting the Knight

description: Whenever a Sarcophagus obstacle is destroyed, it summons a <hyperlink>Skeleton unit</hyperlink> on the defender's side until the end of combat.
name: Haunted Coffins

description: At the start of battle, a couple of War Hound units inflicted with <hyperlink>Berserk</hyperlink> join the fight adjacent to defending units.
name: Escaped Animals

description: All attacking units are immune to <hyperlink>Insanity</hyperlink>.
name: Mentally Stable

description: Every <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink>, 1 attacking unit is targeted; if it has <hyperlink>Low Morale</hyperlink>, it gains <hyperlink>Insanity</hyperlink>, otherwise it loses 10 <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink>.
name: Dead King's presence

description: Become immune to the <hyperlink>Slowed</hyperlink> effect of the Dead King, but start combat <hyperlink>Distracted</hyperlink>.
name: Slow Immunity

description: All attacking units start combat with +4 <defensefrost></defensefrost> <hyperlink>Frost Protection</hyperlink>.
name: Frost Protection

description: This unit is immune to <hyperlink>Insanity</hyperlink>.
name: Insanity Immunity

description: The supporting abilities of attackers give a <hyperlink>Rallying</hyperlink> effect.
name: Rallying support

description: The Dead King inflicts <hyperlink>Slowed</hyperlink> on hits.
name: Lethargy

description: At the start of battle, all attacking units have <hyperlink>Slowed</hyperlink> for 3 <turn></turn>.
name: Slowed Attackers

description: At the start of battle, all defending units have <hyperlink>Slowed</hyperlink> for 3 <turn></turn>.
name: Slowed Defenders

description:
Each 1 , one attacking unit becomes Haunted.

If a Haunted unit stands adjacent to a Sarcophagus obstacle, the Sarcophagus is destroyed and will summon a Skeleton Unit on the defender's side.
name: Stirring Skeletons

description: When this effect expires, any adjacent Sarcophagus obstacle is destroyed and summons a Skeleton <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> unit on the defender's side.
name: Haunted

description: Units that are <hyperlink>Wet</hyperlink> will heal 5 <hp></hp> Hit Points at the start of their turn.
name: Soothing Wellspring

description: Adds <eventColor>{combatproperty}</eventColor> to the battle.
At the start of combat, several <hyperlink>Slowing</hyperlink> Spider Web obstacles are present.
name: Sprawling Spiderwebs

description: When a defending <hyperlink>Magma spirit</hyperlink> is killed, it spawns 1 <hyperlink>Lesser magma spirit</hyperlink>.
name: Magma Split

description: Each time the owner's units suffer damage, they gain 1 stack(s) of <hyperlink>Regeneration</hyperlink>.
name: Spring Growth
spell_description: Adds <hyperlink>Combatproperty fey spring</hyperlink> to the battle.

description: <hyperlink>Combatproperty fey spring</hyperlink> is active in this province.
name: Domain of Spring

description: Attacking units have -1<statuseffectresistance></statuseffectresistance> <hyperlink>Status Resistance</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
Defending units have -1<statuseffectresistance></statuseffectresistance> <hyperlink>Status Resistance</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
All attacking units' attacks deal +10% damage until the end of battle.
name: Strengthened Attackers

description: All defending units' attacks deal +10% damage until the end of battle.
name: Strengthened Defenders

description: At the start of the owner's turn, enemy units adjacent to owner's units have 90% chance of suffering <hyperlink>Burning</hyperlink> and suffer 5 <damageFire></damageFire> <hyperlink>Fire Damage</hyperlink> for each stack of <hyperlink>Burning</hyperlink> they have.
name: Summer Heat

description: <hyperlink>Combatproperty fey summer</hyperlink> is active in this province.
name: Domain of Summer

description: All attacking units have <hyperlink>Sundered defense</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Defenseless Attackers

description: All defending units have <hyperlink>Sundered defense</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Defenseless Defenders

description: All attacking units have <hyperlink>Sundered resistance</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Vulnerable Attackers

description: All defending units have <hyperlink>Sundered resistance</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Vulnerable Defenders

description: Every <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink>, the attacker's units lose 5 morale.
name: The Wailing

description: Killing the Undead Queen will immediately kill all of her [abilityred]Undead Servants[/abilityred].
name: Undead Queen

description: Every 2 <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink>, all Status Effects on all units are dispelled.
name: Wave of Tranquility

description: All attacking units become <hyperlink>Weakened</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Weakened Attackers

description: All defending units become <hyperlink>Weakened</hyperlink> until the end of battle.
name: Weakened Defenders

description: Enemy units suffer 5 stack(s) of <hyperlink>Demoralized</hyperlink> whenever they kill another unit.
name: Winter Sorrow

description: <hyperlink>Combatproperty fey winter</hyperlink> is active in this province.
name: Domain of Winter

description: This <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> has a ranged ability selected. Ranged abilities have an <hyperlink><accuracy></accuracy> Accuracy</hyperlink> rating, which is the chance of the ability hitting the intended target.
description_secondary: If an ability misses, it will either strike another target or do nothing at all. Some abilities can also graze, meaning that the ability affected the target but with reduced strength.
title: Accuracy

description: You have selected a <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>. It has 3 <hyperlink>Action Point</hyperlink> to spend on moving and using abilities.
description_secondary:
Different abilities have different action point costs, and some trigger once per action point available. Using an ability will almost always end a unit's turn!

As you plan movement, you can see the number of action points you will have available at your destination.
title: Action Points

description:
You have temporarily taken command of an Independent army.

While in control of a Free City or <>, you are able to issue orders to their <>. The ability to cast <> is disabled during the Independent turn.
title: Combat Takeover: Independents

description:
You have temporarily taken command of an army belonging to an AI Ruler.

When taking over for an AI Ruler, you can command their <> and make use of their <> during combat.
title: Combat Takeover: AI Ruler

description: This is a Battle Mage <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, which excels at dealing magical damage and applying status effects. It is vulnerable to <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> attacks and should be kept in the back line.
title: <unitBattleMage></unitBattleMage>Battle Mage Units

description: This <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> has suffered <hyperlink>Casualty</hyperlink>. Casualties occur when a unit takes damage, which also causes the unit to deal less damage with its attacks.
description_secondary: Units that are represented by a single figure, such as <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> and giants, are immune to casualties.
title: Casualties

description: Welcome to the field of battle! Here you must kill or rout your foes in order to claim victory.
description_secondary: The defending <hyperlink>Army</hyperlink> always takes the first turn, followed by the attacking army.
title: Battle Commences

description: Your <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> just attacked an enemy from behind. This is called <hyperlink><flank></flank> Flanking</hyperlink>, and gives a damage bonus.
description_secondary: Remember that units in <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink> cannot be flanked!
title: Flanking Attacks

description: You have selected your <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink>. Your Ruler is a powerful combatant who can wield magical equipment and learn a variety of skills.
description_secondary: If your Ruler <hyperlink>falls</hyperlink> in combat, they will return to your <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink> after a short time.
title: <unitRuler></unitRuler>Rulers in Battle

description: A <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> has <hyperlink>Low Morale</hyperlink>, because the tide of battle is turning against it. Units with low morale might <hyperlink>Fumble</hyperlink> attacks, while high morale can lead to <hyperlink>Critical Attacks</hyperlink>.
description_secondary: If a unit's morale drops too low, it will start <hyperlink>Routing</hyperlink> and flee the battlefield.
title: Unit Morale

description: This is a Magic Fighter <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, a front line melee fighter. It specializes in <hyperlink>Magic</hyperlink> attacks, making it ideal for damaging units with high <defense></defense> <hyperlink>Defense</hyperlink> like Shield Units.
title: <unitMagicFighter></unitMagicFighter>Magic Fighter Units

description: This is a Polearm <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, a front line melee fighter. With its <hyperlink>First Strike</hyperlink> and <hyperlink>Charge</hyperlink> Resistance abilities, it is perfectly suited for absorbing enemy <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> attacks.
title: <unitPolearm></unitPolearm>Polearm Units

description: This is a Ranged <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, which excels at dealing physical damage from a distance. It is vulnerable to <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> attacks and should be kept in the back line.
title: <unitRanged></unitRanged>Ranged Units

description: A <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> just got hit by a <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink>. This happens when a <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> unit is struck from within its Zone of Control.
description_secondary: A unit has a limited number of <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink> each turn, shown by red marks under its banner.
title: Retaliation

description: This is a Scout <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, which is weak and best kept out of battle. If forced to fight, its high speed and ranged attacks make it a good unit for <hyperlink><flank></flank> Flanking</hyperlink>.
title: <unitScout></unitScout>Scout Units

description: This is a Shield <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, a front line <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> fighter. When entering <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink>, it grants a bonus to adjacent allies, protecting them against physical damage.
title: <unitShield></unitShield>Shield Units

description: This is a Shock <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, a powerful melee fighter specializing in high-damage <hyperlink>Charge</hyperlink>. Its attacks can cancel <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink>, which makes it strong against Shield Units and Support Units.
title: <unitShock></unitShock>Shock Units

description: This is a Skirmisher <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, which is flexible and uses both ranged and <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> attacks. With its high speed and Slippery ability, it's the perfect unit for hit-and-run attacks.
title: <unitSkirmisher></unitSkirmisher>Skirmisher Units

description: Your Spells are now ready to be cast! Spells can have a variety of powerful effects and can turn the tide of battle when used properly.
description_secondary: Spells are unavailable in the first turn of combat, and require <mana></mana> <hyperlink>Mana</hyperlink> and <optactical></optactical> <hyperlink>Combat Casting Point</hyperlink> to use.
title: Spell Casting

description: This is a Support <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink>, which can use magical abilities to heal and strengthen its allies.
instruction: When entering <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink>, it grants a bonus to adjacent allies, protecting them against magical attacks.
title: <unitSupport></unitSupport>Support Units

description: Your <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> is in an enemy's Zone of Control. When a unit moves into an enemy's zone of control, it becomes temporarily pinned and cannot move for the rest of the turn.
description_secondary:
Moving out of a Zone of Control can trigger an Opportunity Attack.

While in an enemy Zone of Control, many ranged and magical abilities will be unavailable.
title: Zone Of Control

description: Accuracy is the likelihood of attacks landing successfully. If the attack does not land, it misses or grazes the target.<bulletlist><bullet>Grazes deal half damage.</bullet><bullet>Misses deal no damage.</bullet><bullet>Misses can hit random adjacent units next to the target.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: <accuracy></accuracy>Accuracy

description:
Unit use Action Points to attack and use abilities.Units get 3 Action Points per Turn, and can use up to 2 of them to move.

Abilities use action points in different ways:
description_full: Ability costs 3 action points. The unit's turn ends afterwards.
description_full_action_continue: Ability requires 3 action points. The unit retains 1 action point afterwards.
description_leave_one: Ability costs 0 action points. The unit retains 1 action point afterwards.
description_repeating: Ability triggers once per remaining action point. The unit's turn ends afterwards.
description_single: Ability costs a single action point. The unit's turn ends afterwards.
name: Action Point

description:
A base attack is a normal attack that a unit can usually use every turn in combat.

Some Unit Enchantment only affect a unit's base attacks.
name: Base Attack

description: Inflicts <damageBlight></damageBlight> Blight Damage.
name: Blight Damage

description: Blight Protection reduces <damageBlight></damageBlight> <hyperlink>Blight Damage</hyperlink>.
name: Blight Protection

description:
When a Unit sustains damage, members of the unit are lost.

Each member lost lowers the damage output of the unit proportionally. The chance for the unit to apply Negative Status Effect is also reduced.

A Ruler or Hero unit and large monsters only have a single member and are not affected by this rule.
name: Casualty

description:
A Charge attack:Gains extra damage per hex traveled, up to {GLOBAL.ChargeHexes} hexes.Cancels Defense Mode.Removes Retaliation Attack.

These effects are negated by Charge resistance, unless the attack is a Heavymeleestrike.
name: Charge

description: A Heavy Charge attack:<bulletlist><bullet>Heavy Charges ignore <hyperlink>Charge resistance</hyperlink>.</bullet></bulletlist>
A Charge attack:<bulletlist></bulletlist>

charge_shared: <bullet></bullet>Gains <eventColor>{CHARGE_DAMAGE_MULTIPLIER>ResolvedDamageMultiplier}</eventColor>% damage per hex traveled, up to <eventColor>{GLOBAL.ChargeHexes}</eventColor> hexes.<bullet></bullet>Cancels <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink>.<bullet></bullet>Removes <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink>.

description: <bulletlist><bullet>Combat Speed represents how far a unit can move within a <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink> in <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Each hex in combat costs 1 point to traverse.</bullet><bullet><hyperlink>Slowing</hyperlink> terrain costs 2 points to traverse.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Combat Speed

description:
Immune to effects that make you lose control of a unit, such as Berserk and Dominated.
Also grants immunity to being Captured.
name: Control Loss Immunity

description: <bulletlist><bullet>If a unit's attack is a Critical Hit, its damage is increased by +50%.</bullet><bullet>Critical Hits are usually caused by high <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Critical Hit chance can never be higher than an attack's chance to hit.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Critical Hit

description: An ability that attempts to inflict a <hyperlink>Negative Status Effect</hyperlink> on an enemy without directly dealing damage.
Defense reduces damage from <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> and <hyperlink>Missile</hyperlink> attacks.
name: Defense

description: Defense Mode is a <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> ability. When in Defense Mode, a unit:<bulletlist><bullet>Extends its <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink> to all adjacent hexes.</bullet><bullet>Gains +2 <defense></defense> <hyperlink>Defense</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Gains +2 <resistance></resistance> <hyperlink>Resistance</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Is immune to <hyperlink><flank></flank> Flanking</hyperlink>.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Defense Mode

description: While within an enemy's <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink>, a unit is Engaged in Melee and cannot use most ranged attacks or magical abilities.
name: Engaged in Melee

description: Increases chance of <hyperlink>Missile</hyperlink> and ranged <hyperlink>Magic</hyperlink> attacks missing.
name: Evasion

description:
Experience points are earned by units to allow them to reach higher ranks, improving their abilities.

Units earn experience from winning battles. They also earn a small amount each turn on the world map.
Inflicts <damageFire></damageFire> Fire Damage.
name: Fire Damage

description: Fire Protection reduces <damageFire></damageFire> <hyperlink>Fire Damage</hyperlink>.
name: Fire Protection

description: When attacked, a unit with First Strike will use a <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink> to attack first.
name: First Strike

description: Flanking attacks are triggered by attacking a target from behind or from the side.<bulletlist><bullet>Flanking attacks deal +25% damage.</bullet><bullet>Units in <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink> cannot be flanked.</bullet><bullet>If a unit starts its turn in an enemy's <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink>, then it cannot flank it in that turn.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: <flank></flank> Flanking

description: Can only be damaged by abilities or spells that have <hyperlink>Demolisher</hyperlink>.
name: Fortified

description: Inflicts <damageFrost></damageFrost> Frost Damage.
name: Frost Damage

description: Frost Protection reduces <damageFrost></damageFrost> <hyperlink>Frost Damage</hyperlink>.

<bulletlist><bullet>If a unit's attack is a Fumble:<bulletlist></bullet><bullet>A hit becomes a Graze, dealing half damage.</bullet><bullet>A graze becomes a miss.</bullet></bulletlist><bullet></bullet>Fumbles are usually caused by low <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink>.[/bulletlist]
name: Fumble

description:
Each Hero has an Ambition, which sets goals for them to complete and gain Renown. Each includes a Minor Ambition, which can be repeated any number of times, and a Major Ambition, which can only be completed once.

Completing these ambitions grants Renown, while completing the Major Ambition additionally grants a unique hero property.

A hero's Ambition may be changed through an event should that hero fail to complete their goals in a set period of time.
name: Hero Ambitions

description:
Each Hero has a Class, chosen during creation. Each class lets the hero specialize in particular roles and often supports two general variations on that role.

Hero Classes:Hero Class: DefenderHero Class: WarriorHero Class: ElementalistHero Class: RitualistHero Class: RangerHero Class: Death KnightHero Class: Spellblade
name: Hero Class

description:
At certain levels, heroes gain the ability to choose Signature skills. For Champion, Wizard King, and Dragon Lords, these take the form of Affinity Dedications.

Each tier of Affinity dedication becomes available based on the Affinity of your empire and your hero's level:
Initiate - Requires 1 affinity point and a level 4 Hero.Adept - Requires 4 affinity points and a level 8 Hero.Master - Requires 6 affinity points and a level 12 Hero.Paragon - Requires 8 affinity points and a level 16 Hero.


These Dedications grant a benefit of their own and unlock new Hero Skills.

Some Hero types such as Eldritch Sovereigns have special Signature Skills that are not related to affinity.
name: Hero Signature Skills

description:
Each Hero has a Destiny, which sets goals for the hero to complete to gain Renown. Each Destiny has a Minor Ambition, which can be repeated any number of times, and a Major Ambition, which can only be completed once.

Completing Ambitions grants Renown, and completing Major Ambitions grants a unique hero property as well.

A Hero's destiny may be changed through an event should that hero fail to complete its ambitions for a set period of time.
name: Hero Destiny

description:
The Origin is determined by the type of hero made during faction creation; for most randomly encountered Hero this will be Champion.

This is where skills unique to those types are found, such as breath attacks for Dragon Lords or spell enchantments for Wizard King.
name: Hero Origin

description:
Heroes gain Renown as they complete the goals associated with their Ambition. Gaining enough renown increases their Renown Level, which increases the bonuses their Governed City gains from the hero's Governance trait.
Additionally, renown levels grant units in the hero's army additional morale and reduce the chance of losing units when Routing.
name: Hero Renown

description: Compatible weapons:Great WeaponOne Handed WeaponShieldFist WeaponPolearm WeaponSkirmisher Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that specializes in high damage <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> attacks, backed up by <hyperlink>Debuff</hyperlink> and summoned <hyperlink>Undead</hyperlink> units.

description: Compatible weapons:One Handed WeaponShieldFist WeaponPolearm WeaponSkirmisher Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that specializes in defending its allies, survivability, and retaliation.

description: Compatible weapons:Magic Orb WeaponMagic Staff WeaponEldritch Relic Weapon
description_short:
Elementalists are magical damage dealers setting up attacks or delivering the killing blow with powerful Elemental abilities.
Each Elementalist hero chooses a discipline which determines the element of their abilities.

description: Compatible weapons:Ranged WeaponSkirmisher Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that specializes in ranged damage, skirmishing, and disrupting enemies.

description: Compatible weapons:Magic Orb WeaponMagic Staff WeaponEldritch Relic Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that specializes in support through healing and buffs.

description: Compatible weapons:Great WeaponOne Handed WeaponShieldFist WeaponPolearm WeaponSkirmisher Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that uses both <hyperlink>Melee</hyperlink> and <hyperlink>Magic</hyperlink> attacks to deal magic damage from a distance and physical damage when the enemy gets close.

description: Compatible weapons:Magic Orb WeaponMagic Staff WeaponEldritch Relic Weapon
description_short: Warlocks are debuff and undeath experts, using powerful debuffs and empowering undead summons they raise during battle.

description: Compatible weapons:Great WeaponOne Handed WeaponShieldFist WeaponPolearm WeaponSkirmisher Weapon
description_short: A Hero Class that specializes in charge attacks, dealing damage, and gaining strength through fighting.

description: Adept skills are unlocked by acquiring 2 other skills in the same category.
Expert skills are unlocked by acquiring 4 other skills in the same category.
Master skills are unlocked by acquiring 6 other skills in the same category.
A basic hero skill.

<bulletlist><bullet>Hit Points represent the amount of damage a <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> can sustain before it dies.</bullet><bullet>Most units will take <hyperlink>Casualty</hyperlink> as their Hit Points drop.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: <hp></hp> Hit Point

description: Inflicts <damageLightning></damageLightning> Lightning Damage.
name: Lightning Damage

description: Lightning Protection reduces <damageLightning></damageLightning> <hyperlink>Lightning Damage</hyperlink>.
name: Lightning Protection

description: Most ranged attacks need Line of Sight to target an enemy.<bulletlist><bullet>If obstacles or other <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> are between the attacker and the target, the target becomes <hyperlink>Obscured</hyperlink>, reducing <hyperlink><accuracy></accuracy> Accuracy</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Units adjacent to the attacker do not cause a target to be <hyperlink>Obscured</hyperlink>.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Line of Sight

description:
Magic Attacks are attacks performed with magical implements such as orbs and staves.

Many of the special attacks that creatures have, such as dragon's breath, are also considered Magic attacks.

Magic attacks are resisted by Resistance.
name: Magic

description:
Melee attacks are short ranged attacks performed with weapons such as swords, spears, claws and teeth.

They mostly do Physical Damage and are resisted by Defense.
name: Melee

subtitle: -59 to -40 <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink>

description:
Mounts can be equipped by Hero in the relevant slot.
They generally grant Fast movement and a small increase in {}.
Certain powerful weapons cannot be wielded while mounted.
The mount that the Hero starts with depends on their race and any form traits that race may have.
name: Hero Mount

description:
An ability that moves the unit using it to another location.

Cannot be used by units that are Immobilized.
name: Movement Ability

description: <bulletlist><bullet>Move Points represent how far a unit can move within a <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink> on the <hyperlink>World Map</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Normal terrain costs 6 Move Points to traverse.</bullet><bullet>Sometimes the Move Point cost of terrain can be reduced, such as when moving through your <hyperlink>Domain</hyperlink>, but it can never be reduced below 2 Move Points.</bullet><bullet>In <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink> Move Points are not used, <combatspeed></combatspeed> <hyperlink>{LOC.CONCEPT@COMBAT_SPEED@NAME}</hyperlink> is used instead.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: <movementgeneral></movementgeneral> Move Point

description:
A negative status effect is a temporary condition that weakens a unit in some way. They are often applied by << Debuff Spell>> and Debuff abilities.

Examples include:Sundered resistancePoisonedDominatedDecaying

All cultures have a unit ability or spell that can remove negative status effects.

Additionally, some negative status effects have counters—for example, Poisoned can be removed by applying Regeneration.
name: Negative Status Effect

description: Abilities marked with "Can't be refreshed" cannot have their cooldowns and "once per battle" status reset in battle by special abilities such as <hyperlink>Weaver</hyperlink>.
name: Non-Refreshable Abilities

description: When a target is Obscured, it becomes 40% harder to hit with ranged attacks.
name: Obscured

description: <bulletlist><bullet>A unit's Zone of Control is the three hexes in front of it.</bullet><bullet>The Zone of Control blocks enemy movement and determines where the unit can perform a <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Going into <hyperlink>Defense Mode</hyperlink> extends the Zone of Control to all adjacent hexes.</bullet></bulletlist>
Opportunity Attacks are a special type of <hyperlink>Retaliation Attack</hyperlink> that are triggered when an enemy unit leaves the <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink>.
name: Opportunity Attack

description: Inflicts <damagePhysical></damagePhysical> Physical Damage.
name: Physical Damage

description: Physical Protection reduces <damagePhysical></damagePhysical> <hyperlink>Physical Damage</hyperlink>.
name: Physical Protection

description:
A positive status effect is a temporary condition that strengthens a unit in some way. They are often applied by Buff Spell and Support abilities.

Examples include:Bolstered resistanceRegenerationHastenedSteadfast

Certain rare unit abilities and spells can remove positive status effects.

Additionally, some positive status effects have counters—for example, Regeneration can be removed by applying Poisoned.
name: Positive Status Effect

description:
Range refers to the maximum number of hexes away from a unit that an ability can target.
Using attacks on a target at maximum range will often incur an Accuracy penalty.
name: <range></range>Range

description:
Missile attacks are medium to long ranged attacks performed with weapons such as bows or throwing knives.

They mostly do Physical Damage and are resisted by Defense.
name: Missile

description: Resistance reduces damage from <hyperlink>Magic</hyperlink> attacks and <hyperlink>Combat Spell</hyperlink>.
name: Resistance

description: A Retaliation Attack is an attack triggered by another <hyperlink>Unit's</hyperlink> attacks or movement<bulletlist><bullet>Melee units can Retaliate once per <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink> (by default).</bullet><bullet>Attacking an enemy unit within the <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink> triggers a Retaliation.</bullet><bullet>An enemy unit moving out of the <hyperlink>Zone of Control</hyperlink> triggers an <hyperlink>Opportunity Attack</hyperlink>.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Retaliation Attack

description: When a <hyperlink>Unit</hyperlink> moves onto a Retreat Point during <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>, they will immediately exit the battle. <bulletlist><bullet>Nearby friendly units will lose morale <morale></morale>.</bullet><bullet>The unit will lose Move Points <movementwalk></movementwalk> after battle.</bullet><bullet>Retreating your last unit will cause you to lose the battle.</bullet><bullet>If you lose the battle, the unit will either die, or scatter and reappear at one of your cities after a few turns.</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Retreating

subtitle: -60 <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink>

description: Each <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> has an Ambition, this sets goals for them to complete and gain <renown></renown> <hyperlink>Renown</hyperlink>. Each includes a Minor ambition, which can be repeated any number of times, and a Major ambition, which can only be completed once.
name: Ruler Ambition

description: Inflicts <damageSpirit></damageSpirit> Spirit Damage.
name: Spirit Damage
