title: Cave of the Thundershriek: Aftermath

ruler_is_hero: While the troops keep scouting the cavern for remaining enemies, you examine the broken remains of the Thundershriek and its crystal, both masterful creations from a distant age and a clear testament to the magecraft and craftsmanship of the <hyperlink>Ancient Krazura</hyperlink>.

body_footer: "At last, my scouts have tracked the Thundershriek to the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>. There, the secret to its destruction must be hidden. Our war machines are susceptible to its lightning, making me hesitant to send force. So I ask you, 9, will you face and destroy the Thundershriek?"
body_header: "With our reinforcement lines going strong, it is time to discuss a more serious threat, 9."
body_lore: "Without doubt you must have witnessed the Thundershriek," <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> continues, with fervor in <<o:EventPlayer>> eyes. "The terrible creature, half construct, half bird, is the supposed god-protector of Manuhari and descends with lightning, wreaking havoc on our war machines. The <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> say it is immortal and indeed whenever we shot it down, the Thundershriek magically retrieved its own parts and reassembled. I, however, don't believe in immortality."
button_0: "The terror of Manuhari will end!"
title: The Terror of Manuhari

body_footer: "Now that our biggest war machines may safely be deployed again, I want you to have this, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>: it is a reinvention of the Commonwealth's devastating landship, a moving fortress and siege breaker at once."
body_header: With the Thundershriek destroyed for good, <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> is overjoyed to speak to you.
body_lore: "So the Thundershriek was kept alive by the magic of a pristine manacharged crystal? The Oscillator Gem... our Supreme Leader <hyperlink>Edward Portsmith</hyperlink> will be very intrigued to hear of this. In any case, this is a major victory in our war against the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> and we owe it all to you, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!"
button_0: Accept the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> <unit></unit> into your army.
title: The Terror of Manuhari: Aftermath

body_footer: "Eventually our Supreme Leader <hyperlink>Edward Portsmith</hyperlink> grew impatiant and hijacked <<ge:arcane artifacts,the Krazura>> to seek aid beyond Manuhari. This was when the fighting started."
body_header: "Besieging?" <<ge:voice,EventPlayer.FirstName>> trembles with anger. "We were given no choice!"
body_lore: "We arrived on Manuhari as refugees," <<p:EventPlayer>> continues. "Scarred by the <hyperlink>Torment of Shadows</hyperlink> and famished we hoped to find rest at these astral shores. The <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>, however, have acted adversarial since our first contact. We tried to negotiate a permit of settlement, yet their <eventColor>{NativePlayer.TitleName}</eventColor> insisted we should abandon all weapons, which we couldn't."
button_0: "Then you merely defended yourselves! I will grant you my support in this war!"<relationLvl3></relationLvl3>
button_1: "If this is so, you will surely endorse my plans to end this needless bloodshed."
button_2: "Your attempts to frame this incursion as self-defense are pitiful. For the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>!"[relationLvl-3/]
title: The War of Manuhari

body_footer: "I want you to salvage the strongbox from the broken juggernaut, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>. What is inside? Nothing of your concern..."
body_header: "Perhaps." <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> examines you from top to bottom. "But first I must ask you a favor."
body_lore: "The landship which would become the vessel of our misery, housed a strongbox buried deep within the captain's quarters." <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> hands to you a parchment with the technical sketch of a juggernaut. "When we crashed upon Manuhari, much of the landship scattered within the area, and though we tried to scavenge what we could, the site had to be abandoned when the conflict with the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> escalated."
title: Priceless Possession

body_footer: "It seems your intentions are to be trusted, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.FirstName}</eventColor>. Read a scroll from the box, if you fancy, then we may discuss more."
body_header: "You found it!" <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> takes the salvaged strongbox and opens it with a key shard. "Let's see..."
body_lore: "Good... good," <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> swiftly goes through parchment scroll after parchment scroll, most of which simply seem filled with text. "All in good order indeed," <<p:EventPlayer>> concludes, but noticing your questioning expression <<p:EventPlayer>> adds: "War reports from after the opening of Athla's Shadowgate. Most of this is worthless now, but the scrolls were protected by a seal of scrying—had you opened the box to steal or spy I would have known."
title: Priceless Possession: Aftermath

button_0: Study the battle reports <xp></xp> to broaden your tactical knowledge.
button_1: Read of the logistic support <influence></influence> that brought Commonwealth reinforcements to the front lines.
button_2: Examine the incantations <knowledge></knowledge> for conjuring mageslayer weapons.

button_0: "For the sake of peace I will do you this favor."

body_footer: "The headquarters of the 'Deadeye Dragoons' is the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor> <eventColor>{EventDirection}</eventColor> <eventColor>{EventCity}</eventColor>. Kill them. Stage it as infighting. This will restore my authority."
body_header: "What I propose will not be pretty, but at times the ends justify the means."
body_lore: "There is a battalion of hardliners, led by the most ruthless generals of the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>. They barely acknowledge my leadership and foster extreme violence within their carefully picked ranks. If we were to eradicate this battalion, make it look like they cannibalized each other, this would proof the fallacy of their methods and allow me to pronounce a return to <hyperlink>Commonwealth</hyperlink> virtues."
button_0: "You are right. This is not pretty, but necessary."
title: Violent Intentions

body_footer: The all-encompassing voice is searing and maddening, but you can sense its power reaching out to you like a stretched hand, offering itself to be tapped into.
body_header: As your troops are nearing the headquarters of the "Deadeye Dragoons," a surging vision disrupts your thoughts.
body_lore:
"Ignite your fire, {PlayerLeader}...
...the strong, they are rewarded...
...the meek, they burn...
...they trust in their weapons of thunder and steel...
...but you—bear true potential...
...embrace the flame...
...let it guide you to victory!"
button_0: Accept the voice's gift, engaging the "Deadeye Dragoons" in a frenzy.
button_1: Deny the voice and recover your focus before the battle starts.
button_2: Flee.
title: Encountering the 'Deadeye Dragoons'

body_footer: "When the 000003 call for peace, I will answer. As for yourself, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>, any reward I could give shall be yours."
body_header: You have made short work of the "Deadeye Dragoons." <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> applauds you, tense yet visibly relieved.
body_lore: "You did it!" <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> brushes a tear aside, you cannot tell if joyous or sad. "The word of the incident is spreading like a wildfire and it appears the people are buying our version of the story. The path towards old <hyperlink>Commonwealth</hyperlink> ideals will be long and I cannot foresee if I can truly contain the brutality that spread among the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>. But you have given me a fighting chance, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>, and for that I am grateful."
button_0: "When there is peace, I will have my reward <goodact></goodact>."
button_1: "Let me in on the secrets of the Dreadnought <knowledge></knowledge>."
button_2: "Spread my legend <influence></influence> to Magehaven, <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor>."
button_3: "I desire a share of your economic power <gold></gold><production></production>."
title: Violent Intentions: Aftermath

body_footer: "All <hyperlink>Commonwealth</hyperlink> ideals are dead, but there might be a way to rekindle the virtue of my people, return them onto a path of peace."
body_header: "I suppose this is the moment where I need to make a confession, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>."
body_lore:
"I am powerless," {EventPlayer.FirstName} states with a serious voice. "The {EventRace}, they won't obey me if I was to proclaim peace. For long I thought they were simply loyal to Edward Portsmith, but the truth is their loyalties lie with their violent urges alone.

They do not fight to win the war, they fight for the sake of fighting. Just as they loot and plunder for the sake of destruction and reworked their weapons for the sake of cruelty. They no longer resemble the men who stood valiant against Athla's Wizard King onslaught."
button_0: Hear <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> out.
title: The Revelation of <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor>

body_footer: "You have one chance to surrender. Otherwise there will be war!"
body_header: Warning shots and readied <hyperlink>Magelockloreconcept</hyperlink> rifles of soldiers clad in razor sharp armor make it clear, that <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> does not welcome your arrival.
body_lore: "Begone, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.TitleName}</eventColor>! The likes of you are the blight of the <hyperlink>Astral Sea</hyperlink>. Ever hungry for power, you conquer world after world, enslaving and slaughtering the free people of the realms. This ends now! The <hyperlink>Champions</hyperlink> of the mortal races will rally under the banner of a new <hyperlink>Commonwealth</hyperlink>. With war machines and technology we will liberate the cosmos from the dominion of sorcery!"
button_0: "Then let there be war!" <rs_war></rs_war>
button_1: "The invader is you, <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>. I will rise to the defense of the innocent <eventColor>{NativeRace}</eventColor>!" <rs_war></rs_war>
button_2: "You err in thinking all Wizard Kings are malevolent. Allow me to elaborate..."
title: Smoke and Thunder

dragon_ruler: "You err in thinking Elder Dragons are malevolent. Allow me to elaborate..."
edlritch_ruler: "Don't fear what you can't comprehend. The truth about Eldritch Sovereigns..."

body_footer: "The only <eventColor>{EventPlayerType}</eventColor> I would trust is one trapped in a <hyperlink>Cage of Binding</hyperlink>, at my mercy." <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> laughs grimly.
body_header: Your attempt at reasoning with <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> is immediately cut short.
body_lore: "Save your breath!" <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> exclaims. "I have no interest in your lies and attempts to bewitch my mind. Too often have I witnessed the foul influence of poisoned words. The Shadowborn, Emperor Leonus... it's all in the past—a past, that made me stronger. If the <hyperlink>Torment of Shadows</hyperlink> didn't break me, neither will you!"
button_0: Say nothing. You will prove <<P:EventPlayer>> wrong, no matter what it takes.
button_1: Give up on reasoning with <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>. <rs_war></rs_war>
title: Shackles of Trust

body_footer: During this time of timelessness, one recurring thought, strangely so, keeps your mental health intact.
body_header: You are adrift in your mind, surrounded by nothingness.
body_lore: Was it a mistake to enter the <hyperlink>Cage of Binding</hyperlink>? It seems this question might become the torture of your remaining existence. Like an alternate <hyperlink>Torment of Shadows</hyperlink> which exposes you to your inner demons. Forever. Or until <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> decides to end you. The void is all-encompassing, eternal, yet also nowhere and never. You cannot grasp it.
button_0: "I did it all for a noble cause." <goodact></goodact>
button_1: "Without distractions, I can dedicate my mind to unraveling the mysteries <knowledge></knowledge> of the cosmos."
button_2: "When I return, my wrath <xp></xp> will know no equal."
button_3: "My bravery and sacrifice will be immortalized in legends <influence></influence>."
title: Shackles of Trust: Aftermath

body_footer: "I will release you from this terrible isolation, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>. Then tell me what it is you want to talk about."
body_header: All of a sudden a voice reaches out to you, rupturing what could have been a century of isolation: "Let us talk, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>."
body_lore:
"I must admit I am perplexed, {PlayerLeader.Title}." {EventPlayer} reveals <> while glimpsing into your abyss. "You are not what I expected. It would have been easy to seek me out on the battlefield, attempt to eradicate me as a threat. Instead, you chose this—a helpless limbo some may regard as worse than death."

"It makes me question our condemnation of all {EventPlayerType}—and more. When Edward Portsmith ordered the attack on the {EventRace} I had doubts, but trusted his judgment. Perhaps {EventHero.FirstName} was right..."
button_0: "Please explain why you are besieging the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>, <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>."
title: Shackles of Trust: Aftermath

body_footer: "We prevailed through the darkest night, devoid of the light from the Sky Beyond. Now the Serpent has come with thunder and fire, maliciously feigning woe, but whenever it grows a new head, we will peck it out."
body_header: <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> shows no intention of enlightening you on the meaning of <<o:EventPlayer>> words.
body_lore: "What a shameful age to live in, where the ignorant are given the power to challenge the wise" <<p:EventPlayer>> continues <<o:EventPlayer>> speech. "Our forefathers were the sages of the <hyperlink>Sky Beyond</hyperlink>, guides and gate keepers of its many worlds. <hyperlink>The Lion</hyperlink> himself, who ruled above all, sought their counsel and aid against its foes. But when the Lion fought the <hyperlink>World Wyrms</hyperlink>, it became [hyperlink,GLOBAL.ArchonsLoreConcept]the Manticore[/hyperlink], betraying and stinging our ancestors with its poisonous tail."
button_0: "So the Serpent is the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>? I will aid them in their struggle! <rs_war></rs_war>"
button_1: "I am not the Serpent, nor one of its heads! I have come to restore peace..."
button_2: "If we must have war <rs_war></rs_war>, then so be it."
title: Betrayal and Ignorance

silver_tongue: <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> pauses for a moment, indicating a slight courteous movement with <<o:EventPlayer>> head. But <<o:EventPlayer>> words remain bitter.

body_footer: "If you experienced and passed the trial," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> predicts, "the <eventColor>{EventPlayer.Title}</eventColor> will be open for your peace negotiations."
body_header: "There is a ritualistic trial," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> explains, "which anyone aspiring to become the new Yukara has to undergo."
body_lore: "During this trial, the candidate's character will be put to the test by the spirits of <hyperlink>our ancestors</hyperlink>." <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> holds out a silvery feather and leaves it to the wind. "The trial has never been attempted by a foreigner. But the rules do not explicitly forbid it, and I have confidants among the trial wardens, who would ensure that you are allowed in."
button_0: Agree to undergo the trial.
button_1: Decline the trial. As a <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.Title}</eventColor> you have proven <influence></influence> your worth.
title: Trial of the Ancients

body_footer: "I will come to your peace talks," <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> ends her speech, "if you vouch for <eventColor>{TargetPlayer}</eventColor> to attend with honest intentions."
body_header: Having left the last ritual site you are greeted by a more forthcoming <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>.
body_lore: "From the nest of the Serpent," <<p:EventPlayer>> says, "rises the mighty Owl, a herald of the nearing dawn. I have misjudged you, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>, and offer you my apology. The Everdark has left my people vulnerable. A trustworthy and respectful ally will help us redefine our position in the Sky Beyond."
button_0: Thank <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor> and promise to contact <<P:EventPlayer>> once everything is prepared.
button_1: Thank <eventColor>{EventPlayer.FirstName}</eventColor>, but reveal you found the <eventColor>{TargetRace}</eventColor> to be indeed aggressive invaders. You will join the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> in their defensive struggle. <rs_war></rs_war>
title: Trial of the Ancients: Aftermath

body_footer: The warden asks you to leave and return in accordance with the rules of the trial.
body_header: Before your troops comes a trial warden of the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>.
body_lore: "Halt!" <<p:EventUnit>> exclaims with authority. "The ritual site may only be entered by the participant and the participant alone."
button_0: Promise to respect the warden's rules.
title: The Trial Warden

body_footer: "Do you answer the call to arms in this cosmic war that threatens all and everyone?"
body_header: At the ritual site you encounter a <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>, former familiar of the Yukara Zikuta.
body_lore: The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> approaches you, posing a question: "A council is convoked by the guardians of the cosmos. Like all others, your people are called to arms against primal forces. If no one is to send aid, every race may perish. If you come to aid alone, your people may suffer the most."
button_0: Accept the call and face the storm!
button_1: Bribe <gold></gold> the other rulers to accept in your stead.
button_2: Lay out to the council why your people's wisdom <knowledge></knowledge> will aid the cause more than arming them for war.
button_3: Leave the ritual site and return later.
title: Trial of Fealty

body_footer: "You have passed the Trial of Fealty," the familiar says, ending its speech. "May it lead you to a better doom."
body_header: "Valor and responsibility, worthy of a Yukara," the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> proclaims. "Though the sacrifice it demands can be high."
body_lore: "When the <hyperlink>Lion</hyperlink> rallied its lieges against the <hyperlink>World Wyrms</hyperlink>, Yukara Zikuta led a large Krazuran host to the <hyperlink>Sky Beyond</hyperlink>." The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> squawks in a doleful fashion. "But none of her kinsman ever returned and Zikuta became one of the three lost Yukaras whose spirit remained silent during the ancestral rituals."
button_0: Leave the ritual site.
title: Trial of Fealty: Conclusion

bribe_chosen: "A cunning idea," the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> admits. "But would they honor the deal when you couldn't expose them for it?"
knowledge_chosen: "Spoken with a sage's heart," the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> proclaims. "But the sword cuts the quills when there is no shield to defend them."

body_footer: Which part of the doomed realm do you store inside the <hyperlink>Vaultsphere</hyperlink>?
body_header: At the ritual site, you encounter the spirit of <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>, Yukara of the Krazura during the <hyperlink>All-Inferno</hyperlink>.
body_lore: The spirit starts talking to you: "Imagine a realm at the verge of being destroyed by a cataclysmic invasion. All life on the realm will cease to exist and any mark of civilization perish. You have a <hyperlink>Vaultsphere</hyperlink> at your command and enough time to preserve one aspect of the realm for future ages to come."
button_0: The records <knowledge></knowledge> of the realm's history and empires.
button_1: As many civilians as the Vaultsphere can hold. <goodact></goodact>
button_2: Samples from the realm's unique flora <food></food> and fauna <unit></unit>.
button_3: I rally troops for a last stand to save the entire realm! <influence></influence>
button_4: Leave the ritual site and return later.
title: Trial of Wisdom

body_footer: "You have passed the Trial of Wisdom," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> concludes. "A true sage must always doubt."
body_header: "A farsighted decision," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> applauds. "Once, I myself believed this would eternalize all who couldn't be saved."
body_lore: "As the sheer force of the amber <hyperlink>World Wyrm</hyperlink> reshaped Izgemil," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> continues, "I ordered all scrolls, books, and stone plates of the realm to be brought to our <hyperlink>Vaultsphere</hyperlink>. Only when Izgemil had turned silent I realized my unmercifulness and the spirits of Izgemil haunted my conscience for the rest of my life."
button_0: Leave the ritual site.
title: Trial of Wisdom: Conclusion

attack_chosen: "A bold gambit," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> applauds. "Though if it fails, all would be lost."
goodact_chosen: "An act of true mercy," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> applauds. "Even if the rescued souls are a droplet in an ocean of sorrow."
nature_chosen: "A deed of pure preservation," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> applauds. "Though all may wither outside its original habitat."

body_footer: "As the leader of the suffering tribe, how do you preserve unity among your people?"
body_header: At the ritual site, you encounter the spirit of <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>, Yukara of the Krazura during the Everdark.
body_lore: The spirit comes forward to speak to you: "During their darkest age, a once powerful and ancient people stands at the crossroads. Some keep honoring the traditions and knowledge from their civilization's zenith, while others are seeking new ways forward, threatening to cause a schism."
button_0: Persecute the followers of the new ideals to retain common customs and culture.
button_1: Grant the dissidents limited autonomy <influence></influence> if they swear fealty to their brethren in times of need.
button_2: Invoke <mana></mana> the spirits of the past to remind your people of their heritage and legacy.
button_3: ***Root your sages <knowledge></knowledge> in the common population to uphold common virtues and beliefs.***
button_4: Leave the ritual site and return later.
title: Trial of Leadership

body_footer: "You have passed this part of the trial," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> concludes. "May your leadership be a blessing to your people."
body_header: "An approach motivated by benignity." <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> smiles. "I too thought such concessions would preserve peace."
body_lore: "During the Everdark," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> continues, "many movements emerged among the Krazura, each propagating a new dawn for our people. As the Yukara, I feared civil war, allowing new houses to form and adopt their own practices. They remained bound to my lordship through pacts, but over time the respect for those contracts diminished and—after my passing—were broken one by one."
button_0: Leave the ritual site.
title: Trial of Leadership: Conclusion

attacked: "An interesting approach," <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> acknowledges. "But would such unity forced with the sword last for long?"
paid_mana: "An interesting approach", <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> acknowledges. "But sometimes the past can be a burden that not all are able to carry."

body_footer: "I have found a <eventColor>{NativeRace}</eventColor> researcher, <eventColor>{NativeHero}</eventColor>, dedicated to the works of the <hyperlink>Ancient Krazura</hyperlink>. <<Cp:NativeHero>> might be willing to cooperate..."
body_header: <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> comes before you once more, to talk about a matter of great importance.
body_lore: "To restore peace," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> explains, "not only Manuhari should be considered, but also <hyperlink>Edward's</hyperlink> march of destruction across the <hyperlink>Astral Sea</hyperlink>." <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> hesitates, but then continues: "This is not like the <hyperlink>Edward</hyperlink> I knew. I believe—it must be—that something is affecting him, turning him wrathful and blind to reason. Directly before the conflict with the <eventColor>{NativeRace}</eventColor> escalated, Edward was studying some of their artifacts. If I could learn more about their ancient magic..."
button_0: Agree to meet this "<eventColor>{NativeHero.FirstName}</eventColor>".
title: Edward's Insanity

body_footer: "If you were to defeat the ancestral guardians of the structure we call the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, we would be grateful and allow <eventColor>{SorcererHero}</eventColor> to partake in our research."
body_header: "Good ascent, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.TitleName}</eventColor>! I am <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>, chief investigator of the Wing of Lost Wisdom."
body_lore:
"It is excruciating," {EventHero.FirstName} begins <> mournful singsong, "how much knowledge became forgotten by our people during the Everdark, when the stars of the Sky Beyond no longer shone. Which is why the Wing of Lost Wisdom exists: to recover and rediscover the heritage of our ancestors.

Not long ago, we found a grand structure of old Krazuran architecture half buried within the desert. But it was warded by spirit guardians and the {EventPlayer.Title} denied our request for battle mages, giving cryptic answers as is <> custom."
title: Lost Knowledge

body_footer: "I have to thank you, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>, in the name of the Wing of Lost Wisdom and all <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>. As a connoisseur of our fair realm and its inhabitants I offer you a private lecture on a subject of your choice."
body_header: Not long after your troops had laid rest to the spirit guardians of the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> appears at the site in person.
body_lore: "By the beaks of the Seven Sages!" <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> screeches in excitement. "The size of this area and the well-preserved state of the buildings exceed our wildest projections! This is a discovery of immeasurable cultural and historic significance for our people. The Wing of Lost Wisdom has a large task ahead inspecting and processing it all."
title: Lost Knowledge: Aftermath

button_0: Ask for a lecture about <arcana></arcana> adaptive research.
button_1: Let <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> teach you about <nature></nature> survival and recovery in the wilds of Manuhari.
button_2: Hear the discourse about <shadow></shadow> <<ge:interchange,EventHero.FirstName>> of ideas and uncovered historical sites with the minor lords of the realm.
button_3: <<ge:babbling,EventHero.FirstName>> bores you. Ask for some coin <gold></gold> and you will be even!

button_0: Promise <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> to clear out the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>.

body_footer: The guardian spirits seem unaware of your intrusion, but any hasty move will draw their attention. What do you do?
body_header: You enter a grand overgrown structure with a stairway leading up to a portal sphere. Around you, large aureate rings are kept in perpetual movement like a clockwork.
body_lore: Stepping through the portal, you can only presume to be inside the sphere, glimpsing the fragment of another realm. You are in a rocky vale, at the gate of another structure complex of similar architecture, though better preserved. The stairways and buildings seem to lead down to a center square, but the path downward is blocked by looming guardian spirits.
button_0: Charge in without hesitation!
button_1: Weaken their link to the Astral Sea <mana></mana> before attacking.
button_2: Flee.
title: The Eye of Manuhari

no_ruler: The guardian spirits seem unaware of <<ge:intrusion,EventHero.FirstName>>, but any hasty move will draw their attention. What does <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> do?

<eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> enters a grand overgrown structure with a stairway leading up to a portal sphere. Around <<P:EventHero>>, large aureate rings are kept in perpetual movement like a clockwork.

The stairways and buildings seem to lead down to a center square, but the path downward is blocked by looming guardian spirits.

body_footer: Your troops return to you with some items of interest. Which one do you take?
body_header: With the spirits pacified, you make your way down to the center square.
body_lore: At the center rests a large arrangement of circular stone plates, which reminds you of the <hyperlink>World Gate</hyperlink> in <hyperlink>Magehaven</hyperlink>. Any obvious approaches to activating the structure yield no result, however. So you keep exploring the area, which in many ways gives the impression of an abandoned expedition site.
button_0: Take the clearly magical <eventColor>{EventItem}</eventColor> <item></item>.
button_1: Study the void stone tablet inscribed with ancient knowledge <knowledge></knowledge>.
button_2: Activate the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> sphere to summon <unit></unit> a loyal construct.
button_3: We should not desecrate the hallowed grounds of the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>. <goodact></goodact>
title: The Eye of Manuhari: Aftermath

no_ruler: Your troops return to <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> with some items of interest. What does <<p:EventHero>> do?
With the spirits pacified,  makes <<o:EventHero>> way down to the center square.

Any obvious approaches to activating the structure yield no result, however. So <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> keeps exploring the area, which in many ways gives the impression of an abandoned expedition site.

body_footer: "Come to the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>! Together we can solve the mystery of the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>!"
body_header: Pondering the dormant structure inside the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, you are greeted by <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> with relevant news.
body_lore: "You must hear about this, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!" <<p:EventHero>> exclaims, still gasping from the hurry. "The Wing of Lost Wisdom has uncovered a collection of Void Stone tablets. They believe its inscriptions speak of the site and its ancient purpose. However... the tablets are still incomplete and the script is from an early Krazuran age, in need of deciphering and interpretation. Isn't this exciting? It's like a puzzle sent from the past!"
button_0: Promise to send someone along.
title: A Truth Unsealed

body_footer: "I must thank you for your contributions to this important discovery, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>. I bestow upon you the honorary title 'Sage of Lost Wisdom'."
body_header: A euphoric <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> is contacting you from inside the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>.
body_lore: "Pytero xarecha! We did it, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!" <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> evokes an astral reflection of the archaeological site with an activated structure at the center. "This," <<p:EventHero>> proudly proclaims, "is the first of the World Seals, structures used during the <hyperlink>All-Inferno</hyperlink> to shroud the stars of the [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AstralSeaLoreConcept]Sky Beyond[/hyperlink]. That it was hidden within a <hyperlink>Vaultsphere</hyperlink> establishes a clear chronology of first, <hyperlink>Vaultsphere</hyperlink>, then <hyperlink>World Seal</hyperlink>, and lastly <hyperlink>Eternity</hyperlink>, all devised by [hyperlink,GLOBAL.AncientKrazuraLoreConcept]our ancestors[/hyperlink] for <hyperlink>the Manticore</hyperlink> in its need."
button_0: Accept the honors and continue to listen.
title: A Truth Unsealed: Aftermath

body_footer: "I would welcome your insights on the tablets and our working transcriptions, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>. One great mind aids another."
body_header: You are welcomed to the archaeological site by <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>.
body_lore: "Take a look around, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>," <<p:EventHero>> says, pointing to the various tents and work tables populated by fluttering or chattering researchers. "The Wing of Lost Wisdom is making good progress, deciphering and transcribing the Void Stone tablets we discovered. Void Stone was a precious resource even for our ancestors—whatever this structure represented, it must have been of great importance."
title: Investigating the Past

button_0: Personally examine the findings of 55 and <<o:EventHero>> team.
button_1: Leave, for now.
button_2: Delegate some sages <knowledge></knowledge> of your empire to aid the project.
button_3: Let most sages <knowledge></knowledge> of your empire aid the project.
button_4: Have <eventColor>{PlayerHero}</eventColor> aid the project.
button_5: Sharpen your arcane focus to learn the ancient Krazura scripture.
button_6: Connect with the rock and stone at the structure complex to find any missing tablets.
button_7: Commune with the lingering souls of the ancient Krazura to learn more.

no_hero: Have one of your heroes aid the project.

body_footer: "Using this retained knowledge," <eventColor>{EventHero.FirstName}</eventColor> concludes, "I will find and stop <hyperlink>Edward Portsmith</hyperlink>. You have my profound gratitude, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>. Time to share another page from my spellbook!"
body_header: In accordance with <eventColor>{AllyHero}</eventColor>, <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> steps in to continue <<o:AllyHero>> talk.
body_lore:
"This is tremendous; meeting the authentic seal-creators—or, well, their descendants—after everything that happened on Athla... And there is more!"

{EventHero.FirstName} takes a deep breath. "When studying the texts, we found that an activated World Seal does not necessarily block all connections to the Astral Sea. With the right knowledge one can control the Astral Flows, decide who enters or leaves the realm, mold the magic coming through—if only Merlin had known at the time. The history of Athla might have been a different one."
button_0: Ask to be taught <<ge:favorite combat spell,EventHero.FirstName>>.
button_1: Ask to be taught <<o:EventHero>> favorite summon spell.
button_2: Ask to be taught <<o:EventHero>> favorite emergency spell.
button_3: Ask <<P:EventHero>> to share even more insights <knowledge></knowledge> about the World Seals instead!
title: The Seals of Magic

body_footer: The ancestral army of the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> has been sighted at the <eventColor>{EventGeo}</eventColor> <eventColor>{EventDirection}</eventColor> <eventColor>{EventCity}</eventColor>.
body_header: From above the realm's branching treetops, a mechanical shriek announces the attack of the Warden of Manuhari.
body_lore: Imbued with life by the <hyperlink>Ancient Krazura</hyperlink>, the powerful <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> is the god-protector of Manuhari, assaulting trespassers or invaders of the realm without mercy. According to Krazuran myth, it once defeated the obsidian <hyperlink>World Wyrm</hyperlink> and through this achieved immortality.
button_0: Show the "Feather of the <eventColor>{EventPlayer.Title}</eventColor>" to prove your friendship with the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>.
button_1: Let them come.
title: The Warden of Manuhari

body_footer: Will you indeed enter the <hyperlink>Cage of Binding</hyperlink> to astound <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>? Or should you do what is reasonable and instead bend <<P:EventPlayer>> with your might?
body_header: You are alone in a secret chamber of your Wizard's Tower.
body_lore: Before you lies the <hyperlink>Cage of Binding</hyperlink>, a cold dark casing representing the Void. It had not been easy to get hold of it—the secrets of its creation are shrouded in mysteries. Only through a stroke of genius could you conjure the cage from a realm of shadows and horror. And strangely so, it gives you grim satisfaction.
button_0: Enter the Cage of Binding <hp></hp>.
button_1: Return the Cage to the darkness it came from.
title: The Cage of Binding

body_footer: You cast <<P:EventPlayer>> into the <hyperlink>Astral Void</hyperlink> as a testament to what becomes of your foes.
body_header: As the smell of the burning jungle looms over the remaining settlements of the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor>, <eventColor>{EventPlayer.TitleName}</eventColor> lets out a final screech of terror.
body_lore: "The Serpent has bested the Eagle!" <<p:EventPlayer>> cries out in agony. "Our great nests, they lie defenseless. Our heritage—soon devoured. No! I will live on with the next Yukara! My people, they must prevail!"
button_0: Claim the spoils of victory.
title: The Fall of <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>

body_footer: You cast <<P:EventPlayer>> into the <hyperlink>Astral Void</hyperlink> as a testament to what becomes of your foes.
body_header: Amid smoldering war machines and the stinging reek of discharged <hyperlink>Magelockloreconcept</hyperlink>, <eventColor>{EventPlayer.TitleName}</eventColor> is brought to <<o:EventPlayer>> knees.
body_lore: "End this now, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!" <<p:EventPlayer>> screams, like a roaring lion at its last breath. "I am not afraid of death. Whatever comes after this, it will be better than the horrors all <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> had to endure since the invasion of <hyperlink>Athla</hyperlink>."
button_0: Their aggression was their downfall.
title: The Fall of <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>

body_footer: Kept alive by some powerful magic, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> claps its destroyed wings and escapes into the skies.
body_header: The Warden of Manuhari collapses with an ear-splitting blend of crackling astral discharges and squeaking metal.
body_lore: For a brief moment silence ensues, and it appears the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> has exhaled its last mechanical breath. Then however, to the horror of your troops, the broken pieces start moving again, rearranging themselves into a deranged, crooked version of the warden's former self.
button_0: Grimly, you start preparations for the warden's return.
title: Undying Vigilance

description: Before the Fourth Age, when the final World Seal of Athla was opened, the Elven Court and Commonwealth put aside their grievances and made a brave stand against the invading Wizard Kings. In the wars that followed, these heroic alliances crumbled and entire armies were cast into the depths of the Astral Sea.

The Dreadnought Edward Portsmith and the Sorceress Laryssa commanded the vanguard of Commonwealth war machines. After they plummeted into the Astral Sea, they were adrift between worlds, haunted by lurking horrors. Only Laryssa's magic, paired with Edward's resourcefulness, protected the castaways from the magical currents.

After what felt like an eternity of torment, the drifting remnants of the Commonwealth sensed a shift in the currents and happened upon a realm which appeared out of nowhere. The survivors met its inhabitants—an ancient, knowledgeable people called the Krazura. Negotiations were challenging, but the survivors were allowed to recuperate from their trials.

Edward’s mind, however, did not seem to recover. Over time, his resentment toward Wizard Kings grew, and he vowed to free the entire Astral Sea from their curse. He started traveling to other realms to liberate them, leaving devastation in his wake as he condemned and hunted anyone who would support or even tolerate the rule of any Wizard King.

Edward’s erratic behavior concerned Laryssa, his life-long friend and companion during their journey through the Astral Sea. But amidst the growing conflict between the Krazura and Commonwealth Remnants, Edward increasingly ignored Laryssa's pleas, and her influence diminished. Thus it was shortly after Edward’s last departure that Laryssa saw no choice but to send out a secret call for aid, for a Godir who could end Edward’s march of destruction.

description: Thus, by ending the conflict on the Freed Lands of Manuhari, a brave Godir revealed the knowledge about the legendary World Seals. Many Godir had known about the structures which had once obscured Athla itself from the Astral Sea, but only the wizard named Merlin had ever activated them. Armed with the knowledge from the Seals’ very creators, Laryssa Mirabilis continued her quest to stop Edward on his path of destruction.

Answer a call for aid from a sorceress of <hyperlink>Athla</hyperlink>, who has been missing since the <hyperlink>World Gates</hyperlink> were opened. Investigate the fate of the once-powerful <hyperlink>Commonwealth</hyperlink> and the ancient world they discovered.

description: After Grexolis was opened and Sundren’s ruse was revealed, many Godir of Magehaven realized how fragile their alliances were. Sundren's warning of looming evil was drowned out by the clamors of powerful Wizards and Champions, seeking to release the powers from the world vault. Fierce arguments rattled Magehaven, and only its spell of protection kept it from falling apart in its entirety.

Among the Godir of Magehaven, Meandor was one of the few who remained composed. Tired of the bickering within, he had a suggestion: Groups of quarreling Godir would travel to realms where rediscovered Seals had emerged. There, they could settle their differences by competing to become the master of the Seals, without unnecessary bloodshed.

This is the story of one such group of Godir, who decided to settle their disputes on a realm called the Sehiran Oasis.
Little did they know, their trial was about to be rudely interrupted…

description: Thus the dreadnought Edward Portsmith and his war machines were stopped in their tracks. It was revealed that the Endailon of Chaos, released from imprisonment on Grexolis, was amplifying the passion and temper of all Godir. With this proof and newfound understanding, a sense of reason returned to the Godir of Magehaven.

As one of the closest Godir when the Endailon were released, Edward had been the most affected of all. The torment and hatred that had driven him forward had started to cloud his mind until nothing but rage was left, and it was not until his connection to Chaos was severed that he regained his senses. Confronted by the destruction he had wrought, Edward swore to somehow atone for what he had done.

Sundren, meanwhile, did not join her old friends and allies in Magehaven. She traveled onward to search for the Endailon of Chaos and others, guided by the wisdom of her old mentor Merlin before he disappeared.

hero_bio_1:
A proud descendant of the Giant Kings of old, Fjalla carries the responsibility of her royal ancestors on her shoulders. Her father taught her about the beauty of Myrrida, and Fjalla vowed to see its glory reborn.

Fjalla's Jordvolk are proud artisans whose ancestry dates back to the empire of Myrrida, where they served Giant King Thrudgelmir before they pledged their loyalty to his daughter. Under the rule of Fjalla, they honed their craft to perfection, and feel confident of bringing the glory of Myrrida to the Realms once more.
hero_bio_2:
Like many of his kin, Fflammych was born and raised amidst the rivalry between Giants and Dragons. As the guardian of his hearth, Fflammych has seen many a battle and has always protected his kin and people with fire and blood. Recently, however, revelations of greater dangers than Dragons have dimmed the vengeance in his heart. Some say he even dares to question the ancient rivalries.

Fflammych's Hearthkin believe their Souls are forged in the heart of their Giant King, and thus they follow Fflammych with unwavering loyalty. As wielders of the soul-flame, their pyromancers are revered like priests.
hero_bio_3:
As a rumored descendant of one of the Traitor Kings, Singaith seems to have inherited her ancestors' obsession with power and immortality. Reclusive and self-centered, she values knowledge over any form of other fleeting relationship as she schemes for the glory of her kin to rise again.

Like their ruler Singaith and the Traitor Kings of old, the Galetoads are obsessed with achieving eternal life. Through the magic of the Soul and the knowledge of the Eternal Council, they hope to make their eternal dream a reality... through any means necessary.
hero_bio_4:
Hrímis was a Giant serving the ancient [hyperlink,GLOBAL.GiantKingLoreConcept]Giant Kings[/hyperlink] until the Giant Empire of Myrrida fell to the combined forces of Archons and Dragons. Since then, she has been a recluse and avoids any contact with outsiders unless absolutely necessary. Perhaps the encroaching corruption by the Umbral Abyss is one such necessity.

The Kaldbörn are the devoted servants of Hrímis, thriving within the frigid depths of the underground. Much like their Empress, they shun direct conflict, choosing instead to observe from the shadows as great empires crumble.

"Do you feel it? Forbidden magic lingers on this battlefield... Not of creation, but of un-life. My kin tell the story of a Traitor King who cursed the grounds with ancient magics where he fell... None who fought here shall ever know peace. And so, the souls of the fallen remain among their bones, forever fighting, forever dying..."

— Sundren of House Inioch, Memories of the Elven Court

"When I walk among these weathered statues, I ponder the souls they immortalize. Even those whose names are forgotten command my respect. Will I too, be remembered—or forgotten—like this? — Alfred Elderstone, Musings on Rulership

bio_1: In the eras of <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink>, the <hyperlink>Giant King</hyperlink> governed the realms they reshaped in all corners of the <hyperlink>Astral Sea</hyperlink>. But their reshaping did not end with the terrain, as they also modified the inhabitants of the realms the Giants ruled, infusing them with special crystals that made their mortal bodies ageless. The Elder Giants would later use these same crystals to store memories and emotions. Since the fall of Myrrida, the <hyperlink>Eternal Sages</hyperlink> that remain are governed by Eternal Councils.

description:
A crystal formation that replicates Lithorine in an uncontrolled manner.
If left unchecked, they will grow in strength, expand their territory, and send out invasion armies.
lore: A potent garden that grows rock and Lithorite, spewing forth territorial hordes of stone-form aberrations. The Elder Giants of long-lost Myrrida once created and commanded the synthetic organisms colloquially referred to as Lithorine. Defying Nature, the creatures in this garden somehow reproduce their spark of life. Evidently, even synthetic life eventually finds a way.
name: Lithorine Cradle

hero_is_playerle: The escaped <eventColor>{EnemyUnit}</eventColor> notices your warriors. With a snarl, <<p:EnemyUnit>> grabs a nearby <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> and hurls it at you.
Your army follows forceful cracks and crunches to a pond of lava, in which an imposing <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor> was built.

Inside, you find <<a:EnemyUnit>> broken out of <<o:EnemyUnit>> cell, squatting on the prison floor. Dozens of Lithorine creatures who have made their hive in here, crawl around <<P:EnemyUnit>>. The <eventColor>{EnemyUnit}</eventColor> picks up two <<m:EventUnit>> and smashes them into each other. To your bewilderment, and the <<G:entertainment,EnemyUnit>>, the <<m:EventUnit>> reassemble into a <eventColor>{EventUnitB}</eventColor>!

hero_is_playerle: The last of the Lithorine critters crumbles. The <eventColor>{EnemyUnit}</eventColor> lies at your feet, defeated.

The beast finally raises <<r:EnemyUnit>> up and cautiously observes your every action. Will follow <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!"
body_header: With the <eventColor>{CultHero}</eventColor> fallen victim to <<o:CultHero>> hubris, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> returns to the throne room <<p:EventUnit>> once ruled.
body_lore: "<eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> brothers, all dead..." <<p:EventUnit>> says, looking over the bodies of the fallen <hyperlink>Blood Clan</hyperlink> scattered throughout the many chambers of <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>. The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> hangs <<o:EventUnit>> enormous head, <<o:EventUnit>> hideous eyes growing misty. "<eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> fault. <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor> doomed <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>. Showed glory. Brought death. Now <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor> doomed <eventColor>{CultHero}</eventColor>."

There are crystal reflections in the water, blinding your troops, but they vanish again as the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> continues: "The <hyperlink>Giant King</hyperlink> ruled <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink> with great wisdom. There was equality between giants and the smaller kin and even the <hyperlink>Giant King</hyperlink> themselves abided by the law and the verdicts of the <hyperlink>Eternal Council</hyperlink>."
trial_locked: "We have come to judge another <hyperlink>Godir</hyperlink>," the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> exclaims. "Return to us when you have answered in our trials."

body_footer: "The Last Legion is awaiting its orders," the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> speaks. "We are the defenders of <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink>. Speak the word and we will drive off any invaders."
body_header: Examining the Flowrock Artifacts you possess, they suddenly spark alive and within the triangle they form, a <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> rises, pulled from the realm's depths.
body_lore: "You have summoned us to your aid, master?" <<p:EventUnit>> asks, uttering with a mouthless voice. "We have slumbered throughout the ages, lingering in wait below the earth. Is this the day that we finally rise, driving off all invaders that threaten <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink>?" In your mind the images of endless lines of clay soldiers form, opening their lidless eyes within eternal tombs. Their flanks warded by levitating weapons of the old <hyperlink>Giant King</hyperlink> bound by an undying magic.
button_0: Unleash the Last Legion on the realm!
button_1: Say that you will call upon the Last Legion one after one, as actual defenders.
button_2: Relieve the Last Legion from their eternal duty, absorbing the magical essence <mana></mana><bindingessence></bindingessence><bindingfragments></bindingfragments> that kept them alive.
title: The Last Legion: Introduction

body_footer: The Last Legion is rising from its buried chambers of old to assault the realm. How do you wish to prepare for their attack?
body_header: The realm is shaken by fear as doom-tales of a mythical Last Legion of <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink> run rampant.
body_lore: Indeed the earth is in turmoil. You can feel its rippling tremors, hear its ancient murmurs. Villagers from all across the land are telling stories of clay-bound figures moving in the darkness of their fields. Smiths speak of weapons sparking alive and leaving the forges to join the ranks of the Last Legion. The truth of those stories remains to be judged, yet you sense immediate danger.
button_0: "Rally the lieges! <influence></influence> This is the time they shall honor our pacts."
button_1: "Let the heralds <influence></influence> muster any man or woman <unitprod></unitprod> willing to defend our cities!"
button_2: "A Godir fears neither lumps of clay nor rusty weapons."
title: The Last Legion: Stirrings in the Earth

body_footer: Armies of the Last Legion are marching on your cities. Repel their assaults, or all will be brought to naught!
body_header: An unsettling silence falls over your cities as endless lines upon lines of Clay Soldiers rise from the earth.
body_lore: They speak no word, nor do the enchanted weapons floating at their flanks. But it is clear that this Last Legion of Myrrida has only one purpose: to wipe anyone with a footing in their lost ancient kingdom off the realm—except within the lands of <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor>. In this moment of greatest peril the treachery of the <eventColor>{EventPlayer.Title}</eventColor> of the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> becomes clear. It was <<P:EventPlayer>> who unleashed the Last Legion!
button_0: "Once we have bested the storm, <eventColor>{EventPlayer}</eventColor> will pay for this!"
title: The Last Legion: Global Assault

body_footer: In this moment of mournful victory, the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> turn to their <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.Title}</eventColor>. You close your eyes and reshape the scattered clay and weapons into...
body_header: With the Last Legion squashed and beaten, a sense of peace returns to your realm, at last.
body_lore: Yet there is little reason for cheerful victory. For when the foes were only heartless clay and steel, the corpses found on the battlefields too clearly illustrate the losses of your people. There are words speaking of other Godir still standing against the Last Legion in their domains. But it must not concern you, for the <eventColor>{EventRace}</eventColor> are in safety.
button_0: ...a monument of war. <unitprod></unitprod>
button_2: ...a monument of peace. <goodact></goodact>
button_3: ...a mausoleum for the fallen. <influence></influence>
button_4: ...clay workers to rebuild your cities. <structureprod></structureprod>
title: The Last Legion: Fragments of Clay

body_footer: "One battalion is yours to command directly, master," the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> ends. "May you lead us to victory!"
body_header: The Last Legion arrives in terrible splendor as endless lines upon lines of Clay Soldiers rise from the earth.
body_lore: "The hour is nigh, master," a <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> that manifested <<r:EventUnit>> within your throne room speaks. "Today we climb from our deep chambers to defend the vestiges of <hyperlink>Myrrida</hyperlink>. At last our purpose will be fulfilled!" The countless armies of the Last Legion start their march against the other Godir of the realm. Realizing your treachery, they curse your name, yet it is too late.
button_0: "And victory it shall be!"
title: The Last Legion: Glory of Myrrida

bio:
Arvik was a talented necromancer from Athla, standing next to the Elven Court and Commonwealth when his home world was invaded. Together with his people, Arvik was cast into the Astral Void, but the Primal Spirit of the Glacial Mammoth gave him the strength to escape his Torment of Shadows.

The Risen Frostlings originate from Athla, but have since evolved under Arvik's cold rule. They believe power lies in strength of both mind and body, worshiping the resilient Glacial Mammoth as they fight to reclaim their frozen empire once more.

bio:
Birchfoot was never ambitious, but his spiritual visions ensured his rise within Grasshorn society. He is deemed a wise and thoughtful, albeit fretful ruler. When the burden of leadership becomes too heavy, Birchfoot seeks solace in the eye of a thunderstorm, where his connection to the Storm Crow is strongest.

Grasshorns believe themselves to be born from the roots of a lightning bolt, carrying their own likeness of the storms' strikes on their heads. They worship the Storm Crow and see wisdom as their greatest virtue.

Wepwatep was a zealous priestess of the Dune Serpent. So deep was her love for the Primal Spirit, that in an elaborate ritual she had herself covered in snakes and entombed below the shifting sands of the Alkothan Desert. When she emerged, the golden markings of the Dune Serpent were forever etched in her body and soul.

Sandfangs see wealth as a great virtue and adorn themselves in gold and jewelry to honor the Dune Serpent. Priests create pendants of the bones of the dead, for Sandfangs believe it is a great honor to wear the fangs of their forefathers on their bodies.

Serena is a Wizard of Athla and claimed to be master of life, elves and their eternal trees. After her banishment, Serena was tormented by visions of [hyperlink,GLOBAL.WorldsWithinLoreConcept]Worlds[/hyperlink] destroyed by lesser people. Now rooted with religious conviction, she preaches the eradication of those who would threaten the delicate natural balance.

The Verdant Elves are Serena's most loyal followers. The forests are their home, and they will defend it with all their ageless might. They follow the guidance of the Sylvan Wolf and idolize their eerily beautiful Wizard of Life.

nimue_bio: Her mind is a torrent of unpredictable chaos. She wills it, and her children rise from the surge, breathing her very lifeblood. Like the tide beating against the changing coastline, so too is Nimue among the Godir. Her power is undeniable, yet her moods swirl like waves in a tide pool. Her children all accept that, inevitably, all will find themselves drowned in a watery grave.

body_footer: You find yourself between two Godir who fight over nature's domain. With whom do you side?
body_header: Soon after meeting <eventColor>{EventPlayer.TitleName}</eventColor>, <<p:EventPlayer>> contacts you. "Nature's blessings-" <<p:EventPlayer>> starts, but before <<p:EventPlayer>> can finish <<o:EventPlayer>> greeting, <<p:EventPlayer>> is interrupted by <eventColor>{EventPlayer2.TitleName}</eventColor>.
body_lore:
Immediately the two Godir start bickering. "The blessings of Nature Affinity should be protected, not twisted and devolved," {Serena.FirstName} sneers: "All who threaten my domain will be exterminated, even mad 'goddesses' like {Nimue.FirstName}."

{Nimue.FirstName} scoffs. "My {NimueRace} will flood your precious forests. Only the strongest survive the tide, and for that, you must adapt. Allow me to demonstrate, {Serena.FirstName}!"
button_0: Side with <eventColor>{Nimue.TitleName}</eventColor>.
button_1: Side with <eventColor>{Serena.TitleName}</eventColor>.
button_2: Pick no side, let nature (and war) take its course.
title: The Primal Dispute

body_footer: Your people cheer you on as you return to <hyperlink>Magehaven</hyperlink>, victorious.
body_header: You have resolved the conflict between the two bickering <hyperlink>Godir</hyperlink> of <nature></nature> <hyperlink>Nature Affinity</hyperlink>, one way or another. A sense of peace returns to the realm.
body_lore:
Whether this peace will last is unclear. Alliances crumble, friendships change, and the Void twists any mind it touches. In the Astral Sea, few things are eternal.
But for now, the lands of {RealmName} are devoted to your rule.
button_0: Victory is ours!
title: The Primal Dispute: Resolved

bio:
The sands do not regret—they feast. Har'Acran learned that lesson young, when her tribe was plundered. The very raiders who slaughtered her people took her in and raised her. They taught her to survive, to move among the dunes, and to ride upon the scorpions. But they never showed a shred of remorse.

In time, Har'Acran rose to become the Queen of the Dunes, leader of the Sand Stalkers. And she came to understand the raiders, her tribe did not die because of the assault; they died because they could not defend themselves. In the desert, there are only enough resources for those who can take it.

After reclaiming leadership of his tribe on Athla, Ke-nan never ceased his fight against slavery. When the Desert of Kesh was finally freed from the "old ways," the Shatterer of Shackles and his people set out for new worlds. For ages, Ke-nan has wandered across barren realms, freeing those who lived in chains.

The war against the Umbral Demons left a lasting mark on the culture of the Freefolk of Kesh. Embracing magic to empower oneself was seen as an omen of catastrophe; for sooner or later, the thirst for power would corrupt them. In time, these practices became taboo. As the Freefolk of Kesh say: "Sometimes shackles do not clink—they whisper."

As a child who never belonged, Ylac always wanted to learn more about those who should be forgotten. Ignoring the legends and laws of his tribe, he entered a Fractured tower. When he returned home, Ylac was changed. His eyes glowed with a hollow energy, and his mind hungered to know more. But his tribe saw only a monster in the making; and so they cast him out.

The Cursed Wanderers share the affliction that corrodes their leader, one that has only just begun to take shape. Ylac gathered them with promises of power: the power to uncover the source of their affliction, the power to find their place in the world—or the power to reshape the world to fit their image.

body_lore: "Great is the tragedy of the knowledge lost in <hyperlink>the great cataclysm</hyperlink>. Ages have passed, and still no one has discovered that the <hyperlink>Astral Flows</hyperlink> are reversed near the fractures. And that, like any current, they can be navigated and diverted. No one has dared to gaze again into the void of creation. But those who tried... Documented everything. Obey me, and I shall teach you how to decipher their code."

body_lore: These currents surge toward the fissures, siphoning the energy of everything in their path. The Fractures swell as they feed on this power—and then, suddenly, they implode, releasing the devouring winds that are pulled toward the center of the region. "Ruins of the civilization that existed before <hyperlink>the Fracturing</hyperlink>. <hyperlink>Those who condemned this realm</hyperlink> to be devoured by itself. In this city, as in many others, they sought to create something. They experimented with the very origin of magic. And through their arrogance, they tore the fabric of both magic and reality."

body_footer: The source of the contamination is close, you can sense it just beyond the next layer of earth. What were they trying to create with so much mana?

body_lore: The tainted fissures begin to converge toward their source. The energy emanating from them is so intense that you can feel it trying to pull something out from within you. Your troops feel it too, their magic wanes quickly, their enchantments require constant renewal. The energy is draining your mana. How can an energy drain? Whatever experiment the Unmakers conducted... They did it here.
button_0: Prepare your troops to dig.
title: Core of Contamination: Hazard

body_footer: "My tribe... We are the descendants of the Unmakers," says <eventColor>{TribeHero}</eventColor> in shock. "My duty is not over <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>, I shall always guard this place, by your side"
body_header: The <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor> lies before <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor>, finally disconnected from the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, stopping the source of contamination. You see <eventColor>{TribeHero}</eventColor> pick up a journal from the ground.
body_lore: <<Cp:TribeHero>> reads: "A surge of negative magic from the Astral Sea has struck us. We believe an experiment went terribly wrong in another realm. The surge has triggered a chain reaction. The Fractures are erupting, devouring everything in their path. We are trying to shut the experiment down but it is too late, we must seal the city... With ourselves inside. A few will escape, vowing to guard this place forever. They will be called the... <eventColor>{TribeName}</eventColor>.
button_10: Gather as many journals <knowledge></knowledge> as you can.
button_3: Collect the experimental equipment <item></item> of the mages.
button_9: Synchronize with the fractured energy at your own risk <hp></hp>.
title: Core of Contamination: Aftermath

body_footer: It seems that some <hyperlink>Dragons</hyperlink> aided <hyperlink>The Unmakers</hyperlink> to create the <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor>. And that their carcasses roam this place.
body_header: The <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor> swallows energy from the surroundings, feeding something at its core. The pull is so strong that your troops are being depleted of mana.
body_lore: <eventColor>{EventHero}</eventColor> crosses the threshold of the structure. Lifting <<o:EventHero>> gaze to the heart of the tower, <<p:EventHero>> sees it: a miniature <hyperlink>Well of Creation</hyperlink>, the <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor>. Starved for ages, stands a <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>, a majestic creature that once bore a name of its own, now driven mad by the devouring energy. The mages who were trapped within rise beside it, the remnants of the Unmakers.
button_0: Put an end to this experiment.
button_1: Send troops <unitprod></unitprod> to collapse part of the tower onto the Fractured beings.
button_2: Draw protective mana <mana></mana> sigils on your troops.
button_3: Stabilize the mana of your troops.
button_4: Retreat.
button_5: Tap into the cracks of the <eventColor>{EventStructure}</eventColor>, collapsing it over your enemies.
title: Core of Contamination: Fractured Tower
Echoes of the Fracturing: Devouring Winds

body_footer: Whether you seek to stop or wield the destructive power of the <hyperlink>Devouring Winds</hyperlink>, you will find what you covet in the Fated Regions.
body_header: With a tumultuous realm-spanning wave, a <hyperlink>Cataclysm</hyperlink> occurred. Lands turn <hyperlink>barren</hyperlink> in its wake, and spellcasting becomes unreliable.
body_lore: As the dust of this occurrence settles, the devouring energies converge on specific places, lands that existed long before <hyperlink>the Fracturing</hyperlink>. To the nomadic tribes of 51, they are forbidden territory, perilous places full of secrets best left undiscovered. Each fable tells of an <hyperlink>Artifact</hyperlink> of immense power and arrogance, and of a legend claiming that whoever unites three will be able to heal the world... Or to rule it.
button_0: Venture on, in search of these Fated Regions.
title: A Cataclysm Strikes

body_footer: Driven by madness, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> raises the <eventColor>{EventRelic.NoLink}</eventColor>: "Come! Fight me, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>! I know you want this—over my dead body!"
body_header: With <<o:EventUnit>> ghostly host reassembled, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> marches out to complete <<o:EventUnit>> unending siege of <eventColor>{EventCityName}</eventColor>.
body_lore: Yet the deeper <<p:EventUnit>> ventures into the ruined city, the more discontented the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> grows. "Where are those spell-slinging dastards!?" <<p:EventUnit>> shouts angrily, searching for opposition. At last the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> reaches the central crater, silent memorial of <hyperlink>the Fracturing</hyperlink>. Guided by some ghostly intuition <<p:EventUnit>> plunges into the rubble, soon after returning with a radiant object. "What sorcery is this? This cannot be, unless..." The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> gazes directly at you, piercing the Astral veil. "You!" <<p:EventUnit>> screams, "you are an <hyperlink>Unmaker</hyperlink>, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>!"
button_0: Unmaker or not, you will put <<o:EventUnit>> deranged spirit to rest.
title: Phantom Hills: A Mad Truth

body_footer: The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> hands over the <eventColor>{EventRelic}</eventColor>: "The <hyperlink>Unmakers</hyperlink>, they trapped the waters of creation. Yet when they sought to release rain, they unleashed a deluge."
body_header: As <<o:EventUnit>> spirit is about to violently perish, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> is able to finally see the truth.
body_lore: "<<C:<hyperlink>the Fracturing</hyperlink>>>!" <<p:EventUnit>> calls out in dismay, as if <<p:EventUnit>> was reliving the last moments of <<o:EventUnit>> distant life. "All these years—this eternity—I have been... dead." The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> sheathes <<o:EventUnit>> weapon. "I bow to your might and valor, <eventColor>{PlayerLeader}</eventColor>," <<p:EventUnit>> exclaims. "You have ended my vengeful curse and liberated my soldiers. May they all find their peace, at last."
button_0: Before <<p:EventUnit>> vanishes, ask the spirit for <<o:EventUnit>> mark of the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>. <xp></xp><renown></renown>
button_3: Claim the siege engines <unit></unit> of the dissipating host.
button_4: Spread the legend of the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> to inspire instructors <unitprod></unitprod> across your realm.
button_5: Share the tale of the Phantom Hills with the <eventColor>{GLOBAL.EternalSagesLoreConcept.Name}</eventColor>. <allegiance></allegiance>
button_6: Bind <<o:EventUnit>> spirit to your will <unit></unit>, in eternal servitude. <evilact></evilact>
title: Phantom Hills: Aftermath

body_footer: Caught in a long-gone past, the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> commands your troops to prepare for the siege of an already ruined <hyperlink>Unmaker</hyperlink> bastion.
body_header: Entering a fractured wasteland, your troops espy ghostly apparitions straying on the hills. One of them, a formidable <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>, bars the way.
body_lore: "Reinforcements, at last!" <<p:EventUnit>> calls out with brisk fervor. "Those damned <hyperlink>Unmakers</hyperlink> have halted our advance for too long, their unstable magics wreaking havoc left and right. They messed up my soldiers' minds, disabled our siegecraft, infiltrated our positions..." The <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> pauses for a moment, maybe realizing <<o:EventUnit>> words won't inspire much confidence. "With your arrival, the tide has turned. By <eventColor>{EventGodirName}</eventColor>, we will breach their defenses before their magic experiments blast the whole darn realm to oblivion!"
button_0: Let them follow <<o:EventUnit>> delusional orders, for now.
button_3: Persuade <influence></influence> the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> to drill your troops <xp></xp> first.
title: Climbing the Phantom Hills

body_footer: The <eventColor>{EventAnimal}</eventColor> and their horde of wasteland dwellers have infested the <<m:EventStackLeader>>.
body_header: Approaching the inactive siege machines marked by the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor>, your troops start to hear a multitude of clicking and hissing noises.
body_lore:
Carefully observing from a distance, they notice blurry movements within the metallic carcasses of the <>. At last a large {EventAnimal} comes forward, assuming an aggressive posture, while the clickety-clack of <> scissors echoes down the hills.

It is clear that these wasteland creatures, attracted by the still emanated heat of the <>—or their scorpion guise—have made the abandoned siege machines their shelter.

fracture_2_done: The place remains calm, its sigils still glowing with power.
fracture_3_done: The place remains calm, its sigils still glowing with power.

body_footer: "The will of our <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> holds us captive," the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> ends <<o:EventStackLeader>> tale. "We are hapless ghosts, forever chained to a lost purpose."
body_header: On this hill, the lonely ghost of a <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> lingers. As your troops approach, <<p:EventStackLeader>> starts to mumble.
body_lore: "We were positioning all battalions on these hills," <<p:EventStackLeader>> speaks with a stale voice, "ready to descend upon the <hyperlink>Unmakers</hyperlink>. But too late..." The stare of the <<EventStackLeader<eventColor>{man/woman}</eventColor>>> intensifies. "In a flash of teal lightning the city and all its surroundings became torn apart—torn within. We all perished in <hyperlink>the Fracturing</hyperlink>. But it was not the end."
button_0: Leave <<P:EventStackLeader>>, for now.
button_1: "I shall teach you to obey the commands of your <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> beyond death!"
button_2: "Friendship and loyalty <influence></influence> can outlast death. March and your lost purpose will be fulfilled."
button_4: "Rally your troops one last time, and I pledge you shall find peace." <goodact></goodact>
button_5: "The fallen do not question. The fallen obey power."
title: Phantom Hills: Will of the Warlord

morale_restored: The host is ready to assault <eventColor>{EventCityName}</eventColor>.
Returning to the hill, your troops find the ghostly host rallied around the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor>.

Their long lines of armed phantasmal shapes invoke a sense of wonder and terror at once. No eagerness or zeal prevails in their weathered faces, only the fatigue of serving their <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> for a thousand lifetimes.

body_footer: The <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> is feeding on your mana. Whatever information the <eventColor>{EventUnit}</eventColor> is after, you should try to attain it quickly.
body_header: Entering the prison pit of the ghostly encampment, your troops shudder at the sight of the locked-in "spy."
body_lore: "More questions?" the entity's mouth asks, while your men gaze into the abyss of its fractured head. "It's high time. I've been starving... To talk." As the entity speaks you sense an astral pull, its very presence draining your magic. "Ahh," it sighs in relief, "such pleasant... Company. If only I could return to <eventColor>{EventCityName}</eventColor>. With my people... Our <eventColor>{EventRelic.NoLink}</eventColor>, my hunger would cease."
button_0: Flee from the mana drain, for now.
button_1: Confront the entity's shattered memories, reliving <eventColor>{GLOBAL.TheFracturingLoreConcept.Name}</eventColor>.
button_2: Grapple the broken mind <knowledge></knowledge> of the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> to reave <<o:EventStackLeader>> knowledge.
button_4: Squeeze every droplet of mana out of the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> until <<p:EventStackLeader>> squeals.
button_5: Feed the <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor> with an abundance of mana <mana></mana> to mellow <<o:EventStackLeader>> answers.
title: Phantom Hills: Fractured Memories

spy_interrogated: There is nothing more to be learned from this <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor>.
With great caution your troops return to the imprisoned <eventColor>{EventStackLeader}</eventColor>.

<<Cp:EventStackLeader>> seems to have entered a trance-like state, as if the answers you found emptied <<o:EventStackLeader>> mind. Even the astral pull you sensed earlier appears to have subsided, for now.
