description: Tutorial on affinity levels
title: Affinity Levels

description: You can increase your affinity by researching new <hyperlink>Tome</hyperlink>. Higher affinity speeds up unlocking empire skills and is required for high tier Tomes.
Tutorial on your alignment
title: Alignment

description: Your actions have caused your <hyperlink>Alignment</hyperlink> to change. Your alignment represents how others see you, and can affect the base relations value between you and other Rulers and <minorcity></minorcity> <hyperlink>Free City</hyperlink>.
instructions: Alignment ranges from Pure Good to Pure Evil. You can see your current alignment in the bottom right corner, underneath the turn counter. Many alignment changes are temporary and over time will disappear.
title: Alignment

description:
Each Hero has a trait that determines the bonuses they give to the city they are governor of.

A hero’s Ambition shows that hero's personal goals. Helping a hero achieve their ambition grants them Renown, which improves their governance trait.
instruction:
As soon as you get a second city, you can assign your new hero to govern it, so try and choose a hero whose governing style will suit that city.

If you don't have another city yet, it may be worth getting a hero anyway so they can start helping you expand your empire!
title: Hero Ambition and Governance

description: Tutorial on Ancient Wonders found in the world
title: Ancient Wonders

description: This location is called an Ancient Wonder. These structures hold great treasure and bring prosperity to any city that annexes them. But they are often inhabited by powerful creatures.
instruction: An Ancient Wonder can only be explored by a single army led by a Hero.
title: Ancient Wonders

description: Tutorial on Arcane Inspiration
title: School of Potential: Arcane Inspiration

description:
One of your spells has gained its first inspiration, revealing hidden potential!
Potentials are powerful economic effects that can be exploited once the spell has reached full inspiration.
instructions:
Combat Spell gain an inspiration after any combat in which they were cast.
World Spell gain an inspiration any time they are cast.
Check the spell book to view the status of a spell’s inspiration and view the benefit of its potential.

description: Tutorial on exploiting potentials
title: School of Potential: Exploiting Potentials

description: One of your spells has gained enough inspiration to be exploited. While it is being exploited, you gain the benefit of its potential, but lose access to that spell for the duration.
instructions: You can exploit spells with full inspiration from your spellbook by clicking the inspiration indicator to the top-right of the spell icon.

description: Tutorial about your armies on the world map
title: Units & Armies

instruction: Select one of the armies on the map to learn more about them.

description: You have selected an army. Armies are the core of your military strength. They can explore the world, attack your foes, and defend your lands.
instruction: The banners above each army shows what faction they belong to. The panel at the bottom of your screen gives more information about that army.
title: Armies

description: An army can contain up to 6 individual units. You can see a unit's tier, unit role, and movement points in the army panel.
instruction: To learn more about an individual unit's capabilities, <rightmousebutton></rightmousebutton> right-click their portrait in the army panel at the bottom of your screen.
instruction_controller: To learn more about an individual unit's capabilities, press <ci_dpaddown></ci_dpaddown> to go into the army panel, then press <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> on any unit.
title: Army Stack Panel

description: Tutorial on moving your armies over the world map.
title: Army Movement

description: A glorious victory, O <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.Title}</eventColor>! You have beaten an <hyperlink>Army</hyperlink> in <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>, rewarding you with loot and your surviving units with <hyperlink><xp></xp> Experience</hyperlink>. The more experience they get, the stronger your armies become.
objective: You have beaten an <hyperlink>Army</hyperlink> in <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>. You have gained some loot and your units and heroes gain <hyperlink><xp></xp> Experience</hyperlink>. As units survive combat they get stronger and learn new abilities. The higher the <hyperlink>Unit tier</hyperlink>, the more they benefit from <hyperlink><xp></xp> Experience</hyperlink> so upgrade your units regularly.

description: Your armies can move a limited distance every turn. The distance they can move depends on the terrain they traverse.
instruction:
You can move your army by right-clicking on a hex on the world map.

You can control which units in the army move by left-clicking on their portrait.
instruction_controller: While having your army selected, you can move it by pressing on a hex on the world map.
title: Army Movement

instruction: Whenever an <hyperlink>Army</hyperlink> moves onto a hex occupied by enemy army, it initiates <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>. As well as the attacking and defending armies, up to 2 nearby armies for each side can <hyperlink>reinforce</hyperlink> the battle.

description: Tutorial on Army Upkeep.
title: Army Upkeep

description: Beware, O <eventColor>{PlayerLeader.Title}</eventColor>! Your units do not fight for free. They require a certain amount of <gold></gold> <hyperlink>Gold</hyperlink> and <mana></mana> <hyperlink>Mana</hyperlink> each <turn></turn> <hyperlink>Turn</hyperlink>. If you cannot provide these resources, they lose <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink> and eventually desert your army.
Tutorial on Astral Echoes (Attunement)
title: School of Attunement: Astral Echoes

description: You have gained your first <hyperlink>Astral Echoes</hyperlink>. This unique resource is used by School of Attunement Mystics for <hyperlink>Echo Casting</hyperlink>.
instructions: <hyperlink>Astral Echoes</hyperlink> are obtained from Astral Echoes pickups and by researching new skills.

description: Through <hyperlink>Echo Casting</hyperlink> you can cast <hyperlink>Spell</hyperlink> even when you lack sufficient casting points.
instructions:
Combat Spell indicate it in their cost when Astral Echoes are needed to cast the spell. This is automatic once you run out of Combat Casting Point.
World Spell can be manually accelerated by clicking the button on the top left of the priming spell.
title: School of Attunement: Echo Casting

description: Tutorial on Astral Echoes (Summoning)
title: School of Summoning: Astral Echoes

description: You have gained your first <hyperlink>Astral Echo</hyperlink>. This unique resource is used by School of Summoning Mystics for <hyperlink>Echo Infusion</hyperlink>.
instructions: <hyperlink>Astral Echoes</hyperlink> are obtained from Astral Echoes pickups.

description: <hyperlink>Echo Infusion</hyperlink> allows the use of <hyperlink>Astral Echoes</hyperlink> to empower <hyperlink>Magic origin</hyperlink> units by granting them additional ranks.
instructions: The cost of this infusion is based on the remaining <hyperlink><xp></xp> Experience</hyperlink> required before the unit reaches the next rank.
title: School of Summoning: Echo Infusion

description: Some city structures can be <hyperlink>Boosted</hyperlink> to make them cheaper and faster to produce. Check the structure's tooltip to see the boost conditions.
instruction:
Most structures are boosted by having certain Province Improvement in the city's domain, while others are boosted by having a certain amount of Population.

If you boost something that's already in production, you will be refunded the gold you would have saved.
summary: Tutorial on boosting production of city structures.
title: Boosting Production

description: Tutorial on the Bounty Panel
title: Bounty Panel

description: This is the Bounty panel. Here, you can create a <hyperlink>Bounty</hyperlink> to offer it to other <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink>.
instruction: Bounties are quests that are offered to other Rulers in exchange for a reward. Bounties can target <hyperlink>City</hyperlink>, <hyperlink>Infestation</hyperlink> and important structures owned by enemies.

description: Tutorial on camera controls on the world map.
title: Camera Controls

description: Take some time to look around and familiarize yourself with your new surroundings.
instruction: To move the camera around, use the W, A, S, D keys or hold <leftmousebutton></leftmousebutton> and drag your mouse.
instruction_controller: To move your cursor and the camera around, use <ci_leftstick></ci_leftstick>
title: Camera Controls

instruction:
To rotate the camera, hold the middle mouse button and drag your mouse.

Press R to reset your rotation.
instruction_controller:
To rotate the camera, use .

Press to reset your rotation.

description: You can take a closer look at the land by zooming in. Or get a better overview of the world by zooming out. Zoom out far enough to reach the overview map.
instruction: Zoom in and out by scrolling the <middlemousebutton></middlemousebutton> middle mouse button.

description: Tutorial on how to manage your cities.
title: City Management

instruction: To learn more about city management, select your city: <eventColor>{VarThroneCity.Name}</eventColor> on the map.

description: You have selected one of your cities. Cities are central to your economy, and allow you to build more units for your armies.
instruction:
Food, Draft, and Production are resources used to develop your cities.

Gold, Mana, Imperium, and Knowledge are resources that can be spent on any city, unit or spell.
title: Managing your cities

description:
Location and Province Improvement located in a city's domain will provide you with income.

Structures can be also be built to provide extra income, as well as unlocking units and boosting the city's defenses.
instruction:
Select the hammer button located in the right side of the city panel and choose a structure to build.

Recommendation: Build a {VarCityUpgradeTwo} or {VarCityUpgradeOne}.

description: Cities also recruit your units. Units cost <hyperlink>Upkeep</hyperlink> every turn, so keep an eye on your income to ensure you can pay for your units.
instruction:
Select the helmet button located under the production queue and choose a unit to recruit.

Your faction's Scout unit is the {VarScoutUnit}

description: Tutorial on City Cap
title: City Cap

description: You are close to reaching your maximum number of cities. Acquiring more cities than your maximum will result in major economic penalties.
instruction: You can increase your <hyperlink>City Cap</hyperlink> via the Empire Development Tree or you can continue to grow your empire by making newly acquired cities your <hyperlink>Vassal</hyperlink> instead.
title: City Cap

description: Tutorial on annexing new provinces to your cities
title: City Expansion

instruction: Select a city that has increased its population.

description: This city has grown and gained a new <population></population> <hyperlink>Population</hyperlink>. Each additional population enables you to expand the city's domain by placing a <hyperlink>Province Improvement</hyperlink>.
title: City Expansion

description: Every <hyperlink>Province</hyperlink> has different features which determine what type of improvement can be built in it.
instruction:
Click on the pin button to add the province to your city's domain.

Remember that provinces with Resource Node will give you more income.
instruction_controller: Select the pin button <province></province> in the city panel to start selecting a province and improvement to build there.

description: Tutorial on city production.
title: City Production

description: Tutorial on starting combat with hostile armies
title: Starting Combat

description: You are about to enter combat. Inspect all participants and their combined strength before deciding if you want to fight manually or have your army automatically fight the battle.
instruction: If you use Auto Combat, the fight will be simulated and you will be able to replay the battle yourself if you don't like the results.
title: Combat Preview

description: Cities without defending <hyperlink>Army</hyperlink> are vulnerable, but building <hyperlink>Walls</hyperlink> will force attackers to besiege a city giving you valuable time to bring in reinforcements.
instructions:
Building Palisade walls will grant basic protection to your new cities and unlock more advanced defenses such as the Caltrop stash and Archer battlements.

Your Throne City starts with {GLOBAL.STRUCTURE_UPGRADES.PALISADE_WALLS} already constructed.
summary: A tutorial about defending your cities
title: Defending Your Cities

description: Tutorial on diplomatic interactions with other Rulers
title: Diplomacy

objective: Open the Diplomacy screen with another player.

description: You have encountered another <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink>. They will be your biggest roadblock to victory. But they may also prove to be powerful allies.
title: Diplomacy

description: This overview will show you in-depth information about another Ruler: their personality, <hyperlink>Treaty</hyperlink> and current <hyperlink>Relations</hyperlink> with you.
instruction: Inspect the other Ruler and decide if this is someone you wish to forge an alliance with, to defeat... Or anything in between.

description: Tutorial on Prison and Crypt and Embalmed Sacrifices
title: Cult of Death: Prison & Crypt and Embalmed Sacrifices

description: A defeated hero has been put in your prison or crypt. You can either hand them over to their rightful owners for a reward, or if they are in your crypt, embalm them to gain <hyperlink><embalmedsacrifice></embalmedsacrifice>Embalmed Sacrifices</hyperlink>. You may execute heroes in your prison to move them to the crypt.
instructions:
As the Cult of Death, you may use Embalmed Sacrifices to build powerful City Structures or cast Morbid sacrifice.
Upgrading your Wizard Tower in the Throne City will unlock City Structure that grant additional benefits to the prison and crypt.

description: Tutorial on gaining empire skills
title: Empire Skills

description: This is the empire development tree. Here you will specialize your empire towards certain play styles. Increase your empire's <hyperlink>Affinity</hyperlink> to open more options.
instruction: Learn about each empire skill by hovering over it.
title: Empire Development

description: You will progress toward unlocking your next empire skill every turn, depending on your <hyperlink>Affinity</hyperlink> values. Unlocked skills can be obtained by spending <influence></influence> <hyperlink>Imperium</hyperlink>.
instruction: Most skills provide passive bonuses, but some skills provide you with a one time bonus like resources or units.

description: Tutorial on enchanting units
title: Enchantments

description: You have just researched a <caststrategic></caststrategic> <hyperlink>Unit Enchantment</hyperlink> spell. These spells allow you to empower your armies. They apply to all units with a specific role and cost upkeep for each unit affected.
instruction: In order to use the enchantment you'll need to cast it. You can do this from the Spell Book.
instruction_controller: In order to use the enchantment, you'll need to cast it. Press <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> to open the radial menu and select the <spellbutton></spellbutton> Spells button.
title: Unit Enchantments

description: Race transformations will cost a lot in terms of resources. The changes they make are more drastic and powerful and cannot be reversed. Your entire race will evolve into something... more.
title: Transformations

description: Tutorial on Feudal Houses (Aristocracy)
title: Feudal Aristocracy: Feudal Houses

description: You have just founded a <hyperlink>Feudal House</hyperlink>, this is a unique entity for the Feudal Aristocracy to manage.
instructions: The assigned Governor is now the <hyperlink>Liege lord</hyperlink> of this House, any units produced in this city or summoned into armies of this House will likewise become part of their House and gain benefits from fighting alongside their Liege!

description: As the House's <hyperlink>Liege lord</hyperlink> gains <renown></renown> <hyperlink>Renown</hyperlink>, units of that house gain <hyperlink><xp></xp> Experience</hyperlink> and the <hyperlink>Liege lord</hyperlink>'s effect increases.
instructions: Field units of each House alongside their <hyperlink>Liege lord</hyperlink> to drastically reduce their upkeep and increase their effectiveness!

description: Tutorial on interacting with Free Cities
title: Free Cities

description: You have encountered a free city. They are independents that can be vassalized, integrated or conquered.
instruction: Inspect the Free City and give them a <whisperingStone></whisperingStone> <hyperlink>Whispering Stones</hyperlink> to start building a relationship with them.
title: Free Cities

description_primary: In the following steps, you will create your people, followed by your Ruler.
description_secondary: For your first faction, we suggest you focus on the theme instead of the numbers; role-play your favorite trope or go crazy with experimentation!
name: Faction Creation
recommended: <recommended></recommended> Each tutorial will suggest a good option, if you’re unsure what to pick.

description_primary: In this step, you can customize your faction further to control how your faction acts when under AI control.
description_secondary:
This section allows you to create a list of city names for your faction to use, as well as to create extra heroes who you will be able to recruit as the game progresses.

It also lets you control how the AI will behave when it controls your faction, letting you control the tomes it will research and the way it will behave diplomatically.
name: Faction Creation: Advanced Settings

description_primary: In this step, you will pick your people’s culture, which defines your starting units and economy.
description_secondary:
Some cultures have subcultures that have slightly different units and mechanics.

The icons ( ) next to the culture names are called Magic Affinities, reflecting your people’s attunement to 6 cosmic forces. Your affinity score has a big impact on your playstyle!
name: Faction Creation: Culture
recommended: <recommended></recommended> Feudal - Monarchy is an easy to play culture where your Ruler gives bonuses to their units in battle.

description_primary: You’re nearly done, all that’s left now is to name your Ruler and race, and you can begin!
description_secondary: If you wish, you can also change your Ruler's <hyperlink>Ambition</hyperlink> or look at the Advanced Settings which let you customize your race even further, but we recommend that you leave that for later once you’ve had time to familiarize yourself with the game itself!
name: Faction Creation: Finalize

description_primary: In this step, you can choose your faction’s physical form, which controls how they look and affects their performance in battle.
description_secondary: Each form has its own set of traits, which affects their abilities in battle as well as the types of terrain they find comfortable and if they can ride special mounts. If you don’t like a Form’s default traits, you can always change them to something else!
name: Faction Creation: Form
recommended: <recommended></recommended> Humans are an easy to play form that develop quickly and are resilient to damage.

description_primary: In this step, you can pick an ambition that your Ruler can fulfill in order to earn bonuses that affect your throne city.
description_secondary:
Each ambition has 2 objectives for your Ruler to fulfill. A major one that can only be completed once, and a minor one that can be completed repeatedly.

Fulfilling ambitions grants Renown, which strengthens the bonuses your Ruler grants to your starting city.
name: Faction Creation: Ruler Ambition
recommended: <recommended></recommended> Instructor is a simple ambition which you fulfill by accompanying your units in battle.

description_primary: In this step, you can change how your Ruler looks, as well as their class, which determines their abilities in battle.
description_secondary:
Once you’ve chosen a class, you can choose which equipment your Ruler will start with. You can always change your equipment later in game, as long as the new equipment is compatible with your class!

The rest of the choices only affect your appearance, and the appearance of your race’s units. Feel free to pick whatever you wish, it will have no impact on your stats or economy.
name: Faction Creation: Ruler Appearance
recommended: <recommended></recommended> The Warrior is a powerful class, focused on melee combat and survivability.

description_primary: In this step, you will start to create your Ruler, a powerful hero who accompanies your armies and carries out your will!
description_secondary: The Ruler origin grants a number of economic bonuses to your empire, as well as determining the kinds of abilities they have in combat.
name: Faction Creation: Ruler Origin
recommended: <recommended></recommended> The Champion is a good choice for a strong starting army and a large throne city.

description_primary: In this step, you will pick two society traits, which shape how your race plays on the world map.
description_secondary:
Each society trait gives an economic bonus that rewards a particular playstyle, as well as a small starting bonus that helps you when the game starts. Some also affect your race’s starting Alignment, which has a big impact on how rival empires view you.

Like cultures, your society traits also affect your Magic Affinity!
name: Faction Creation: Society Traits
recommended:
Gifted Casters makes it easier to cast spells.
Fabled Hunters increases the rewards you get from battles.
Prolific Swarmers strengthens early game units.

description_primary: In this step you will pick a starting Tome—a collection of magical spells, units and bonuses that you will be able to research to empower your empire.
description_secondary:
A tome represents a path that your race will follow as they develop through magical research. They contain spells, units, and enchantments you can use to empower and even transform your people!

You will be able to choose more tomes later in the game, once you’ve researched enough skills.
name: Faction Creation: Tome
recommended: <recommended></recommended> The Tome of Pyromancy has a good selection of powerful fire spells, as well as 2 <unitBattleMage></unitBattleMage><hyperlink>Battle mage</hyperlink> to reinforce your armies.

description_primary: On this screen you choose where your grand adventure will begin. You can choose a premade realm for a unique experience, or create a realm of your own to explore!
description_secondary: <bulletlist><bullet>Story Realms have extra narrative, telling the saga of Magehaven and the Astral Sea.</bullet><bullet>Challenge Realms have special rules and mechanics for experienced players.</bullet><bullet>Unknown Realms have randomized, hidden traits that you discover as you play and are not for the faint hearted!</bullet></bulletlist>
name: Realm Selection
recommended: <recommended></recommended> For your first adventure, the Fields of Rebirth is a relaxing introduction to the game.

description_primary: Here you can create your own realm in the Astral Sea for you to explore. You can choose how many other Rulers will be present, as well as how powerful they are.
description_secondary:
Customize Realm lets you select a number of realm traits—these are advanced settings that can radically change how a realm plays. You can change the realm’s geography and inhabitants, as well as adding special rules or victory conditions.

Advanced Settings gives you even more control about how your realm is configured and the rules that govern how the game functions.
name: Realm Setup
recommended: <recommended></recommended> For your first adventure, it is not recommended that you add any traits to the realm.

description: Tutorial on city governors
title: Governors

description: You have opened the governor assignment menu. Here you can see all available <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> that can become the governor of this city, along with the bonuses they would provide.
title: Governors

description: Tutorial on declaring wars and the grievances required to justify them
title: Declaring War & Grievances

description: You have just gained or caused a <casusBelli></casusBelli> <hyperlink>Grievance</hyperlink> against another Ruler. These are used to justify wars. You could also forgive them to improve your <hyperlink>Relations</hyperlink>.
instruction: Your wars need to be justified, otherwise they are considered <evilact></evilact> evil. Your <hyperlink>War Justification</hyperlink> is determined by both your <casusBelli></casusBelli> <hyperlink>Grievance</hyperlink> and those of the other Ruler. They can be inspected by hovering over the <casusBelli></casusBelli> icon in the diplomacy overview.
title: War Declaration & Grievances

description: Tutorial on what you can do with heroes and how to get additional ones.
title: Rulers & Heroes

instruction: Select an army with a hero and <rightmousebutton></rightmousebutton> right-click the hero portrait to inspect that hero. A silver army banner signifies an army led by a hero. A golden army banner signifies an army led by a special hero: your Ruler.
instruction_controller: Select an army with a hero, press <ci_dpaddown></ci_dpaddown> to go into the army panel, then press <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> to inspect that hero. A silver army banner signifies an army led by a hero. A golden army banner signifies an army led by a special hero: your Ruler.

description: You have selected a hero. Heroes lead your armies around the world. Only they have the authority to explore <hyperlink>Ancient Wonder</hyperlink> and start <hyperlink>Siege</hyperlink>. They can also construct <hyperlink>Outpost</hyperlink> in order to <hyperlink>Found Cities</hyperlink>
instruction: Level up heroes by using them in <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink> and equip them with items you find as loot.
title: Rulers & Heroes

description: Tutorial on selecting skills when a hero levels up
title: Hero Level Up

description: One of your <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> has gained a level! This grants them a skill point they can spend on a hero skill from one of their skill trees.
instruction: Select your hero and open the level up screen from the unit panel to view your available hero skills.
title: Hero Level Up

description: Tutorial on opening the hero skill trees
title: Hero Skill Trees

description: On this panel, you can acquire new skills to upgrade your hero, granting them new active abilities as well as powerful passive bonuses.
instruction: A hero gains a new skill point each time they level up. Every few levels they also gain a <hyperlink>Signature Skill</hyperlink>, which unlocks new skills and grants a bonus skill point.
title: Hero Skill Trees

description:
Here you can recruit a new Hero, if your Hero Cap is high enough. Your hero cap increases over time, but you can spend Imperium to increase it immediately.

Heroes from your own realm are always available, but heroes from the Free City you meet can also appear.
instruction: <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> who originate from other <minorcity></minorcity> <hyperlink>Free City</hyperlink> have their own race, granting them different bonuses and abilities.
title: Hero Recruitment

description: Tutorial on Hostage Diplomacy (Cult of Tyranny)
title: Cult of Tyranny: Hostage Diplomacy

description: The Dark Subculture "Cult of Tyranny" uses heroes in their prison to take control of Free Cities and exploit Vassals.
instructions: <bulletlist><bullet>Defeated <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> belonging to <minorcity></minorcity> <hyperlink>Free City</hyperlink> become Hostages in your <hyperlink>Prison</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Hostages provide <hyperlink><allegiance></allegiance>Allegiance</hyperlink> every turn and count as an assigned <whisperingStone></whisperingStone> <hyperlink>Whispering Stones</hyperlink>.</bullet><bullet>Conquered Cities released as Vassals also immediately grant you a Hostage.</bullet><bullet>When Vassalizing a city that belonged to another <hyperlink>Empire</hyperlink>, all <hyperlink>Hero</hyperlink> of that empire in your prison become hostages of this new Vassal instead.</bullet></bulletlist>

description: Tutorial on hostile Free Cities
title: Hostile Free City

description: You have encountered a hostile <minorcity></minorcity> <hyperlink>Free City</hyperlink>. They are independents that can be vassalized, integrated or conquered.
instruction: This city is at <rs_war></rs_war> <hyperlink>War</hyperlink> with you. You can defeat them through conquest, or negotiate a peace, after which you can give them a <whisperingStone></whisperingStone> <hyperlink>Whispering Stones</hyperlink> to start building a relationship with them.

description: Tutorial on Imperium
instructions: Imperium income can be increased by building parts of your Wizard Tower in your <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink> or by annexing <hyperlink>Ancient Wonder</hyperlink>.
title: Imperium

description: You have gathered a large amount of <influence></influence> <hyperlink>Imperium</hyperlink>. This represents the influence you have over the world. You can use it to acquire new cities, unlock new <hyperlink>Empire Skill</hyperlink> or speed up city growth.
instruction: Imperium is mainly gained by building parts of your <hyperlink>Wizard Tower</hyperlink> in your <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink> or by annexing <hyperlink>Ancient Wonder</hyperlink>.
title: Imperium

description: Tutorial on infestations
title: Infestations

description: An infestation is close by. Invading armies will be sent from its spawner location to your lands if left unchecked for too long. Destroying them, however, might prove challenging.
title: Infestations

description: Tutorial on the Item Forge
title: Item Forge

description: This is the Item Forge, where you can forge new items for your Heroes. Making items costs <bindingfragments></bindingfragments> <hyperlink>Binding Fragments</hyperlink>, which you gain by disenchanting the Items in your Arsenal.
instruction:
Higher tier items also cost Binding Fragments, which can only be gained by disenchanting higher tier items.

You can empower your items with Infusions to grant them special properties. You can get access to more infusions by collecting Magic Material. Collecting more of the same material will unlock more powerful infusions.
title: Item Forge

instruction:
Each Infusion has a point cost. The total amount of points used determines the tier of the item. Higher tier items:Cost more {GLOBAL.BindingEssenceConcept.Name}.Take longer to craft.Do more damage (in the case of weapons).

Only one item can be crafted at a time. If you cancel crafting, all resources spent will be refunded.

description: Tutorial about lava provinces found on the world map.
title: Lava Provinces
tutorial_description: You have discovered a lava province. You can annex lava provinces to grow your empire, but doing so will negatively affect your <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>City Stability</hyperlink>. Only units with specific properties will be able to traverse lava.
tutorial_instruction:
The City Stability penalty can be avoided by having either the Underground or Desolate Adaptation.

You can build the Mine and Conduit Province Improvement in this sector.

Flying movement and Floating movement units can traverse this sector without any issues, but land walking units will need Lava walk.

description: Tutorial on the various locations found on the world map
title: Locations

description: You have encountered a <hyperlink>Resource Node</hyperlink>, they provide additional yield to the <hyperlink>Province</hyperlink> they are located in.
instruction: To gain the benefits of this node, you will need to <hyperlink>Annex</hyperlink> its province to one of your Cities.
title: World Map Locations

description: You have found an army of Marauders; these often guard important locations and grant a reward when destroyed.
instruction: Not all neutral armies are the same. An army bearing the tower banner represents a Free City. A black banner with a skull signifies a Marauder Guard. The Red banner with a skull signifies an army belonging to an Infestation.
title: Marauder Guard

description: Tutorial about low food income in cities
name: Low Food Income

description: <food></food> <hyperlink>Food</hyperlink> income in one of your cities is running low, this means your city will grow more slowly and may eventually lead to <hyperlink>Starvation</hyperlink>!
instructions:
Each Population in the city eats some food, so you need to ensure the income increases as the city grows.

To increase your city’s food income:Annex provinces with Pastures.Build Farm province improvementsBuild Food giving city structures like 0000048 and {VarCityUpgradeTwo}.

description: Tutorial explaining how to deal with low <gold></gold> gold income.
title: Low Gold Income

description: Your empire’s <gold></gold> <hyperlink>Gold</hyperlink> income is getting very low. If you run out of gold, your units will lose <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>Morale</hyperlink> and may even desert!
instruction:
Unit Upkeep is a common cause of low gold income, so you may want to disband some units if you have too many.

To increase your gold income:Annex provinces with Gold Veins.Build Mine province improvements.Build gold giving city structures like {VarCityUpgradeOne} and {VarCityUpgradeTwo}.

description: Tutorial explaining how to deal with low <mana></mana> mana income.
title: Low Mana Income

description: Your empire’s <mana></mana> <hyperlink>Mana</hyperlink> income is getting very low. If you run out of mana, you will not be able to cast spells!
instruction:
Unit Enchantment Upkeep is a common cause of low mana income, so you may want to cancel any active Unit Enchantment you have.

Magic origin units, like Spirits, Fairies, and Skeletons cost mana each turn, which may also be a cause.

To increase your mana income:Annex provinces with Mana Nodes.Build Conduit province improvements.Build mana giving city structures like 0000048 and {VarCityUpgradeTwo}.

description: Tutorial explaining how to deal with low <eventColor>{GLOBAL.CityStabilityConcept.Name}</eventColor>.
name: Low City Stability

description: <happiness></happiness> <hyperlink>City Stability</hyperlink> in one of your cities is running low, this will reduce the city’s income and may eventually lead to more serious issues unless you fix it.
instruction:
City Stability drops as a city annexes more provinces and may also be caused by invading enemies or narrative events.

To increase city stability, try building a or {VarCityUpgradeTwo}, which are unlocked by building the {VarCityUpgradeThree}.

description: Tutorial on magic materials
title: Magic Materials

description: You have selected a magic material. These have various unique effects if acquired via annexation or through trade. Gathering all materials from a category will yield a powerful empire-wide bonus.
title: Magic Materials

description: A tutorial about independent armies.
title: Marauders

description: Tutorial on negotiations between Rulers.
title: Negotiation

description: Negotiations are mutually beneficial agreements with fellow <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink>. You can propose <hyperlink>Treaty</hyperlink> to strengthen the bond between your empires, you can <hyperlink>Trade</hyperlink> assets to make a profit, or you can send gifts to improve <hyperlink>Relations</hyperlink>.
title: Negotiation

description: Tutorial on notifications and ending the turn
title: Notifications & Ending Turns

description: Deal with all notifications to ensure no important tasks remain unattended. Then, you can safely end your turn.
instruction: <leftmousebutton></leftmousebutton> Click the notifications on the right to go through them or skip them with <rightmousebutton></rightmousebutton>.
instruction_controller: Use <ci_righttrigger></ci_righttrigger> to go through the notifications in order. The list can be opened using <ci_dpadright></ci_dpadright>, allowing you to skip notifications with <ci_buttonx></ci_buttonx>.
title: Notifications & Ending the Turn

description: Tutorial on settling new outposts
title: Outposts

description: Tutorial on the importance of outposts
title: Outposts

description: Outposts solidify your control over a region. You can use them as a safe place to recuperate, to lay claim to the surrounding lands, and they can also be turned into cities.
instruction:
Outposts can only be built by heroes standing on the center of a province.

Outposts can collect resources of the Location within its Domain similar to cities. Its defenses can be upgraded to help protect your claimed land.
title: Outposts

description: Tutorial on using the Overview Map
title: Overview Map

description: You have reached the overview map. As you explore the world, you will have many threats and opportunities to consider. Use this to inform your strategies.
instruction: Zooming back in will get you back to the regular view.
title: Overview Map

description: Tutorial on pillaging provinces and the ruins that remain
title: Pillaging & Ruins

description: When you are inside of the domain belonging to your enemy, you can pillage their <hyperlink>Province Improvement</hyperlink> to gain resources.
instruction: Move an army onto a <hyperlink>Province Improvement</hyperlink> and select the "Pillage Province Improvement" button.
title: Pillaging Provinces

description: Tutorial on the prison and crypt in your Throne City
title: Prison & Crypt

description: A defeated hero has been put in your prison or crypt. You can either hand them over to their rightful owners for a reward, or you can keep them there for now.
instruction: Upgrading your <hyperlink>Wizard Tower</hyperlink> in the <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink> will unlock <hyperlink>City Structure</hyperlink> that grant additional benefits to the prison and crypt.
title: Prison & Crypt

description: Tutorial on the Quest Panel
title: Quest Panel

description: This is the Quest Panel. Here, you can review your progress on Victory Conditions, Quests, and Bounties.
instruction: From this panel you can abort quests, or track them to keep their current objectives visible when the panel is closed.

description: Tutorial on the Rally of the Lieges
title: Rally of the Lieges

description: Something is available in your <hyperlink>Rally of the Lieges</hyperlink>. To access your Rally of the Lieges, select the button from the top bar.

You have opened the Rally of the Lieges overview. Here you can rally armies from your <hyperlink>Vassal</hyperlink> and conquered <hyperlink>Ancient Wonder</hyperlink>. The amount of units you can rally is determined by how many vassals and Ancient Wonders you own.
instruction:
A rally happens regularly. This can be sped up by spending Gold.

You can come back to the Rally of Lieges at any time before the next rally starts to recruit more units.
title: Rally of the Lieges

description: Tutorial on selecting tomes and researching their skills
title: Research

instruction: Open the Arcane Research screen with the button on the top left of the screen.
instruction_controller: Open the Arcane Research screen by opening the radial menu using <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> and selecting the tome icon.

description: Arcane research enables you to learn new <hyperlink>Spell</hyperlink> and acquire new units. The culture and <hyperlink>Tome</hyperlink> you have chosen for your faction determine the initial skills you can unlock through arcane research.
instruction: Choose one of the skills that seems the most useful to you.
title: Arcane Research

description: Your empire will research the skill over time using your <knowledge></knowledge> <hyperlink>Knowledge</hyperlink> income. Once the research is completed, you will choose between three new skills.
instruction: Every time you research 5 things, you will unlock a new <hyperlink>Tome</hyperlink> to research things from.

description: Tutorial about your Ruler dying in battle.
title: Your Ruler has fallen!

description: Your <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink>, <eventColor>{RulerDead.Name}</eventColor>, has perished in <hyperlink>Combat</hyperlink>, this is a setback but all is not lost! They will return from the void in 3 turns at your <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink>.
instructions:
While your Ruler is gone, you will not be able to cast Spell, progress Research, or do Diplomacy.

Additionally, if you lose your Throne while your Ruler is in the void, you will lose the game!

description: Tutorial on Seals
title: Seals

description: You have encountered a Seal. These structures can be captured to achieve a <hyperlink>Seals Victory</hyperlink>. They are guarded by powerful defenders that will attack any who claim their Seals.
instruction: There are multiple Seals in a world, and each one that you claim contributes <eventColor>{amount1}</eventColor> point every turn, the first <hyperlink>Empire</hyperlink> to reach the predetermined amount is victorious. Every <eventColor>{amount2}</eventColor> turns, seal defenders will spawn to retake their Seals. They increase in strength as you approach victory, so be prepared to fight for them.
title: Seals Victory

description: Tutorial on laying siege to cities
title: Sieges

description:
You have started a Siege on this city. It takes a number of turns to breach the city's walls, depending on its Fortification Health.
The following assault may be bloody, but a city is a valuable prize when captured.
instruction: To influence the duration of a siege, you can pick <hyperlink>Siege Project</hyperlink> on the bottom left of the siege screen. These can speed up the siege or destroy enemy defenses to make the upcoming battle easier.
title: Laying Siege

description: Tutorial on special improvements
title: Special Improvements

instruction: Special Improvements can be built in your cities. Go to the production list of one of your cities.

description: You are about to build a special province improvement. These must be built on top of existing improvements. They provide better economic bonuses and are often affected by the provinces around them.
instruction: Select a province you want to build this special province improvement on.
title: Special Improvements

description: Tutorial on priming and casting spells
title: Spellcasting

instruction: To access your spells, select the blue button next to your Ruler in the bottom right.
instruction_controller: To access your spells, open the radial menu with <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> and select the <spellbutton></spellbutton> Spell icon.

description: This is your spell list. You can cast various spells from here to bolster your units and cities, or to smite your enemies.
instruction:
When you select a spell, you pay its Mana cost and start to cast it. A spell will take a number of Turn to cast depending on its cost in World Map Casting Point, the more casting points you have the less time this will take.

Some spells, such as Unit Enchantment cost Spell Upkeep each turn. You can review your ongoing spells under the Active tab.
title: Spells

description: Stability measures how happy the people in your cities are. Outside of Dark Cultures which do not suffer from low stability penalties, you generally want to keep your stability high.
instructions: You can find the stability of your cities by hovering over the <happiness></happiness> mask symbol next to the city name in the city interface.
title: City Stability

description: Tutorial on Thralls
title: <thralls></thralls> Thralls

description: As an Eldritch Sovereign, you can enslave Thralls, who can be sacrificed to cast ritual <hyperlink>Spell</hyperlink>. Thralls are enslaved automatically when you are victorious in battle.
instructions:
The more and stronger enemies you fight, the greater the chance and amount of thralls gained.

You can learn more ritual spells by acquiring certain hero skills as your Ruler levels up.

description: Tutorial on the Throne City
title: Throne City

description: You have selected your <hyperlink>Throne City</hyperlink>. Your Throne City is the most important city in your <hyperlink>Empire</hyperlink>.
instructions:
Your current Throne City is {VarThroneCity}. This is where you can build your Wizard Tower and where your Ruler will reappear when <> perishes.

If you lose both your Throne City and your Ruler, you are defeated.

You can relocate your throne to any other city through the City Information screen.

description: You can open the Encyclopedia to find information about various units, mechanics, or spells.
instructions: The button is located in the top right corner of the screen, marked by <tow></tow>.
instructions_controller: To open the Encyclopedia screen:<bulletlist><bullet>Press <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> to open the radial menu.</bullet><bullet>Choose the <inspect></inspect> button.</bullet><bullet>Choose the <tow></tow> button.</bullet></bulletlist>
title: Encyclopedia

description: Tutorial on selecting tomes and advancing in arcane research
title: Tome Selection

description: You have acquired enough arcane skills to choose a new <hyperlink>Tome</hyperlink> to add to your research library. Additional tomes will expand the selection of arcane skills available to you.
instruction: Every Tome grants a collection of spells, units, and other upgrades to research. Read the summaries and pick a Tome that fits your play style.
title: Tome Selection

description: For every two tomes you pick, you will unlock the next tier of tomes. Higher tier tomes also require a certain amount <hyperlink>Affinity</hyperlink> to be unlocked.
instruction:
The Tome Library in the research screen shows the complete collection of tomes as well as what is needed to unlock them.

The cost of a tome's skills depends on the number of tomes chosen beforehand—each tome’s skills are more expensive than the ones before them.
summary: Tutorial about unlocking higher tier tomes
title: Tome Progression

description: Tutorial on the use of hyperlinks and tooltips.
title: Hyperlinks & Tooltips

description: You can always find out more about a topic if you ever need more information to inform your decisions.
instruction: You will often find a <hyperlink>Hyperlink</hyperlink> in text. Hovering over one will show important information about a concept or system. Hover your mouse over the underscored word "Hyperlink" above to open a tooltip.
instruction_controller: You will often find a <hyperlink>Hyperlink</hyperlink> in text. Hovering over one will show important information about a concept or system. Move your selection over the underscored word "Hyperlink" above and use <ci_options></ci_options> to go into the tooltip.
title: Hyperlinks & Tooltips

description: Tutorial on Race Transformations
title: Transformations

description: You have just researched a <caststrategic></caststrategic> <hyperlink>Race Transformation</hyperlink> spell. These powerful spells alter a race of which you are a <hyperlink>Keeper</hyperlink>, granting them powerful permanent bonuses.
instructions:
Major Transformations are exclusive, so each race may only have one. Minor Transformations are weaker, but have no such limitation.

In order to use the transformation, you'll need to cast it. You can do this from the Spell Book.
instructions_controller:
Major Transformations are exclusive, so each race may only have one. Minor Transformations are weaker, but have no such limitation.

In order to use the transformation, you'll need to cast it. Press to open the radial menu and select the Spells button.

description: Tutorial on the Underground layer
title: Underground

description: This is the <hyperlink>Underground</hyperlink>. It is rich in minerals and <hyperlink>Ancient Wonder</hyperlink>. As long as you have access to a passage, you can freely move between the surface and the underground.
instruction:
The Excavation Empire Skill is useful for navigating the underground by removing diggable earth. This can sometimes hide treasures or marauder armies ready to attack and pillage your cities. Races with the Underground Adaptation trait fare better in the Underground.
To leave the underground you can click on the layer button in the top right corner.
instruction_controller:
The Excavation Empire Skill is useful for navigating the underground by removing diggable earth. This can sometimes hide treasures or marauder armies ready to attack and pillage your cities. Races with the Underground Adaptation trait fare better in the Underground.
To leave the underground press .
title: The Underground

description: When a <hyperlink>Province</hyperlink> containing an Underground Passage is <hyperlink>Annexed</hyperlink>, the city may use the passage to expand to the other layer.
instruction: Some <hyperlink>Magic Material</hyperlink> are more common underground, while others may be more common on the surface.
title: Expanding through Passages

description: Tutorial on how to use the Unit Panel to get information on each unit.
title: Unit Information

description: You have selected a unit and opened the unit panel. This panel shows the details on a unit and what the unit is capable of, as well as any weaknesses you could exploit.
instruction: You can hover over the icons to learn more about a unit's abilities, passives and unit types.
title: Unit Panel

description: Beware! You are engaging combat with a high tier unit. A <hyperlink>Unit's Tier</hyperlink> is shown in the bottom left of their portrait in the army panel.
instruction: The higher a unit's tier, the more dangerous they are. <rightmousebutton></rightmousebutton> Right-click on their portrait to investigate them further, and prepare accordingly—or rethink this combat.
instruction_controller: The higher a unit's tier, the more dangerous it is. Press <ci_rightbumper></ci_rightbumper> to go into the army panel, then press <ci_buttony></ci_buttony> on any unit to investigate it further and prepare accordingly—or rethink this combat.
summary: Tutorial over fighting higher tier units.
title: Unit Tiers

instruction:
Victory can be claimed through the Expansion Victory, Magic Victory, Score Victory or Military Victory.

You can click on each victory to see detail of its conditions and your progress.

description: Tutorial on the types of victory conditions
title: Victory Conditions

description: There are many paths to becoming the Ruler of this realm. Some may wage war, but others may take a more peaceful approach.
title: Victory Conditions

description: Tutorial on War Bounties
You can now create a <hyperlink>Bounty</hyperlink> to request aid in your war! Bounties are quests created by <hyperlink>Ruler</hyperlink> and offered to other Rulers in exchange for a reward.
instruction:
Go to the Quests panel on the top-left to create a bounty. There, you can also find bounties you and other Rulers have posted and bounties you have accepted.

Bounties can target City and important structures owned by enemies.
title: War Bounties

description: An introduction message
title: Welcome to Age of Wonders

description: A new Age of Wonders dawns.
instruction:
Allow me to lend some aid, O {PlayerLeader.Title}. During play, messages like this will provide advice on how to achieve victory on this realm. Some of these will trigger objectives for your growing empire.

Click on the button on the bottom right to open additional advice, and reread any tutorials you've already completed.

You can disable the tutorial in the settings menu.
instruction_controller:
Allow me to lend some aid, O {PlayerLeader.Title}. During play, messages like this will provide advice on how to achieve victory on this realm. Some of these will trigger objectives for your growing empire.

You can get extra information and reread completed tutorials by opening the radial menu with and selecting the Advice option.

You can disable the tutorial in the settings menu.
title: Welcome to Age of Wonders!

description: Tutorial about healing armies outside of combat.
title: World Map Regeneration

description: Some of your units have lost <hyperlink>{<hp></hp>}</hyperlink> and will need some time to regain them.
instruction:
Each unit regenerates a certain amount of health each turn. Moving the unit back into your Domain speeds this process up, while staying in enemy domain or near an Infestation will slow it down.

You can still fight while your units are damaged, but they might be weaker due to having Casualty.
